a318.speaker: Amakan, Mimi Errol and Christelle Mangoua - respectively art critic, painter and curator of the tribute exhibition (press conference of 27 February)
a318.name: Amakan
a318.title: Mimi Errol and Christelle Mangoua - respectively art critic, painter and curator of the tribute exhibition (press conference of 27 February)
a318.speech: Announced that “a well-deserved tribute will be paid to the artist through an exhibition whose opening will take place on Thursday 7 March, from 6:30 p.m., at the Museum of Civilisations of Côte d'Ivoire,” running from 7 to 21 March under the theme “Monné Bou: the mystery of the throw, 50 years on,” under the patronage of the Minister of Culture and Francophonie, Françoise Remarck, and set out its three parts: a documentary display of the artist's diplomas and gallery photographs, a presentation of photographs of works by age bracket to show the evolution of his plastic writing, and a conversation between Monné Bou and the younger generation through the work of young artists such as Amakan.

a318.speaker: Mimi Errol, art critic, speaking for the organisers
a318.name: Mimi Errol
a318.title: art critic, speaking for the organisers
a318.speech: “After half a century of contemplating the beauty of Monné Bou's works, we are still questioning ourselves about the mystery hidden behind his throwing technique.”

a318.speaker: Christelle Mangoua, curator of the tribute exhibition
a318.name: Christelle Mangoua
a318.title: curator of the tribute exhibition
a318.speech: “At Adiaké, where we visited him to tell him about our project, I was pleasantly surprised to see that Monné Bou has documented his work very well since 1973. Since his first exhibition in Marseille. He gave us several items, even administrative ones, and photos of his works to help us follow his career... And when we began to go through the documents, the theme of this tribute exhibition imposed itself. And for us, given the quality of his work, there was no question of going in the direction of a simple exhibition. We are therefore going to present the man: Monné Bou, the artist, his work from yesterday to today. We had long dreamed of putting the video projectors on the artist and the particularity of his working technique.”

a406.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, UDF leader
a406.name: Atupele Muluzi
a406.title: UDF leader
a406.speech: Confirmed his intention to be on the ballot in 2025, emphasizing that Malawians will vote for him to lead the country as President.

a406.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, UDF leader
a406.name: Atupele Muluzi
a406.title: UDF leader
a406.speech: Said key focus areas include food security, energy, export promotion, education reform, tourism revitalization, and healthcare, with a strong emphasis on ensuring Malawi becomes food secure.

a406.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, UDF leader
a406.name: Atupele Muluzi
a406.title: UDF leader
a406.speech: Emphasized that Malawi has enough resources to generate wealth, advocating for innovative thinking and establishing a Sovereign Wealth Fund to reduce reliance on foreign aid.

a406.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, UDF leader
a406.name: Atupele Muluzi
a406.title: UDF leader
a406.speech: Proposed a new leadership style where the President is seen as a servant, not a boss, encouraging citizens to address him as “Mr. President” instead of “His Excellency.”

a406.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, UDF leader
a406.name: Atupele Muluzi
a406.title: UDF leader
a406.speech: Said the UDF is not considering alliances at the moment, intending to independently contest and serve Malawians; reflected on past alliances as limiting voter choice.

a406.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, UDF leader
a406.name: Atupele Muluzi
a406.title: UDF leader
a406.speech: Criticized the exploitative Thangata system where poor farmers are disadvantaged, and promised to end this cycle and introduce policies to protect and empower smallholder farmers.

a406.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, UDF leader
a406.name: Atupele Muluzi
a406.title: UDF leader
a406.speech: Dismissed criticism of his uncontested candidacy within the UDF, comparing it to global examples like Donald Trump's nomination in the Republican Party, asserting it reflects the will of the people.

a406.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, UDF leader
a406.name: Atupele Muluzi
a406.title: UDF leader
a406.speech: Encouraged Malawians to vote based on hope and a vision for better governance rather than anger or frustration.

a406.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, UDF leader
a406.name: Atupele Muluzi
a406.title: UDF leader
a406.speech: Acknowledged the lessons from UDF's loss in 2020 and his own temporary resignation, stating that he used the time to travel, learn, and return with renewed insights to serve Malawi.

a406.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, UDF leader
a406.name: Atupele Muluzi
a406.title: UDF leader
a406.speech: While recognizing his family's political legacy, emphasized his independence and the importance of learning from past leaders while addressing contemporary challenges.

a477.speaker: Kova Zoumanigui, President of the Court for the Repression of Economic and Financial Offences (CRIEF)
a477.name: Kova Zoumanigui
a477.title: President of the Court for the Repression of Economic and Financial Offences (CRIEF)
a477.speech: In a decree published today, justified the suspension of hearings by the holding of the training session for Guinea's lawyers scheduled for 13-14 November in Conakry, as well as the 2024 solemn opening session of the Guinean Bar, to be held from 11 to 15 November ; specified that this suspension is exceptional and that it will not affect the handling of judicial cases in the long term.

a477.speaker: Decree of the CRIEF (official document)
a477.name: Decree of the CRIEF (official document)
a477.speech: States that the suspension concerns all CRIEF hearings during the period from 11 to 15 November; that consequently no judgment will be handed down and no new proceedings will be initiated during that week, and that litigants with ongoing cases must wait until 18 November 2024, when hearings will resume normally at 9:00 a.m.

a477.speaker: Article 47 of the Guinean Code of Civil, Economic and Administrative Procedure (legal text)
a477.name: Article 47 of the Guinean Code of Civil
a477.title: Economic and Administrative Procedure (legal text)
a477.speech: Allows the president of the CRIEF to extend or suspend procedural deadlines in cases of force majeure.

a491.speaker: Analysts
a491.name: Analysts
a491.speech: View the development as a calculated attempt by the group to counter the federal government's narrative that paints the militants as barriers to modernization and technological advancement. The strategic loosening of restrictions may be intended to portray Al-Shabaab as more tolerant and in tune with younger generations, particularly in contrast to the government's perceived failures.

a491.speaker: International observers
a491.name: International observers
a491.speech: Warn that the country – particularly the capital Mogadishu – risks following an "Afghanistan-style" trajectory.

a703.speaker: Tabora United players (anonymous, names withheld on request)
a703.name: Tabora United players (anonymous
a703.title: names withheld on request)
a703.speech: Told Mwananchi that they decided to go on strike over their unpaid salaries for May and June. "We have been making a lot of noise about this but the officials are not showing any cooperation, which has made us unite and strike until they pay or listen to the important needs we require," said one of the players. ; The player said that playing was not a problem for them because it is their job, but what they want is to see the leaders take their needs seriously, because they have families and various people who depend on them to make a living. ; "This matter started with some of the technical bench from the beginning, who have also been leaving for reasons of this kind and the management does not take it with great seriousness, so we players have also decided to take this decision," said that player.

a703.speaker: Charles Obiny, Chief Executive Officer of Tabora United
a703.name: Charles Obiny
a703.title: Chief Executive Officer of Tabora United
a703.speech: Said he cannot discuss matters circulating online because for now their goal is to ensure they finish the two remaining matches well. "If there is an issue of non-payment being talked about, it has not yet reached my desk, and if it exists we as management will issue a statement; also, when someone has a claim he cannot use striking as a basis but should follow the proper procedure," said Charles.

a703.speaker: Richard Abwao, Chairman of Tabora United and Tabora Regional Police Commander
a703.name: Richard Abwao
a703.title: Chairman of Tabora United and Tabora Regional Police Commander
a703.speech: Said they have had to hold a meeting with the players to put things right before starting the trip to face Azam. "Right now we are in a meeting with the players to discuss various internal matters of the team before starting the journey to Dar es Salaam to play Azam," said the official.

a733.speaker: African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) (press release)
a733.name: African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) (press release)
a733.speech: Officially confirmed that three individuals survived the military helicopter crash that occurred on Wednesday morning at Aden Abdulle International Airport in Mogadishu, and that the survivors were immediately transferred to the AUSSOM Level II hospital for medical treatment; according to the press release, search and recovery operations are ongoing to locate and assist the five remaining individuals who were on board at the time of the crash.

a733.speaker: Somali Civil Aviation Authority (SCAA)
a733.name: Somali Civil Aviation Authority (SCAA)
a733.speech: Has also confirmed that an investigation has been launched to determine the cause of the incident, that the crash site has been secured, and that aviation experts are currently gathering evidence to support the inquiry.

a733.speaker: Airport authorities (Aden Abdulle International Airport)
a733.name: Airport authorities (Aden Abdulle International Airport)
a733.speech: Emphasised that safety protocols were promptly enacted and that airport operations remain stable and uninterrupted.

a788.speaker: Nona Deprez, EU Ambassador to Liberia
a788.name: Nona Deprez
a788.title: EU Ambassador to Liberia
a788.speech: Speaking at the official signing ceremony, expressed delight to have finally signed the financing agreement for European Union budget support to the Republic of Liberia; said the 56 million euros grant is in direct support to the budget and 7 million euro grants for complementary measures, with the ultimate goal of increasing Liberia's autonomy with less dependency on external financing sources: "The European Union's use of direct budget support reflects our confidence in the Government of Liberia's commitment to pursue ambitious reforms, promote accountability and improve financial governance, and this funding modality demonstrates a strong partnership and shared goals between the European Union and Liberia in promoting good governance and sustainable development" ; said the complementary-measures project is foreseen to be managed by the Swedish International Development Agency (SIDA), comprising work streams on improved public finance management systems and domestic revenue mobilization, including natural resources, and stronger accountability and transparency for civil society and better capacitated audit systems.

a788.speaker: Nona Deprez, EU Ambassador to Liberia
a788.name: Nona Deprez
a788.title: EU Ambassador to Liberia
a788.speech: Disclosed that the signing of the financing agreement was a culmination of many months of engagements, conversations, discussions and negotiations with the Government of Liberia, and extended appreciation to all ministries, agencies and commissions engaged in the discussion: "We know this is only the start of the journey, because now the real work starts, so we need to keep on engaging very regularly until the Government of Liberia can submit a disbursement request, hopefully still this year, so that hopefully we could still disburse about 22 million euros maximum into the treasury in 2025" ; noted the reforms are to strengthen public finance management and oversight systems, enhance domestic revenue mobilization particularly from the natural resources sector, improve transparency and accountability, create a more conducive business environment for investment in local rice value chains, and reinforce Liberia's network of protected areas ; "So we look forward to continue to work with you, so that this program can be a successful indicator of the achievement and the implementation of Liberia's ambitious reforms."

a788.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a788.name: Augustine K. Ngafuan
a788.title: Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a788.speech: Thanked the EU envoy and her team on behalf of President Boakai and the citizenry and praised the EU for standing alongside Liberia during its difficult times: "I want to say again, on behalf of President Joseph Nyuma Bokai and the government, the people of Liberia, to say thank you to the EU family. You've been a friend, indeed. We are at pivotal times. We've been facing some turbulence and some trumps" ; "in some respects, some of our partners have been backpedaling on commitments, cancelling commitments. But you are front pedaling on commitment; you are delivering on commitment. And in one instance, where one of our partners was stepping down on support, you were stepping up on support. So, I want to say thank you on behalf of the Liberian people who remember you. You are doing for us so that we can do for ourselves." ; "You are doing it for Liberia, and we as a government will try as much as possible to be worthy recipients of the support."

a788.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a788.name: Augustine K. Ngafuan
a788.title: Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a788.speech: Said the ultimate aim of the government's ARREST agenda is to transform lives of people across the 15 counties; noted that the EU support is a grant, not a loan, for three years, and that the budget support comes directly to the government budget: "It is a vote of confidence in the reform that we've initiated, working in partnership with the EU and other partners. We have agreed indicators, and we have a policy dialogue framework that we take very seriously." ; said the government wants to reach a point where the people can depend largely, almost 100%, on their own resources for development: "We are on that path. Last year, of the $738 million budget, we raised $698 million through domestic resource mobilization. So, that was upwards, I think, of 90%. So, we intend that the government's contribution to the budget will continue to increase, as we expand the tax base through a package of measures, including principally improving efficiency."

a791.speaker: Siaka Diakité, President of the National Organisation of Coffee-Cocoa Producers of Côte d'Ivoire (Onpcc-CI)
a791.name: Siaka Diakité
a791.title: President of the National Organisation of Coffee-Cocoa Producers of Côte d'Ivoire (Onpcc-CI)
a791.speech: Expressed his gratitude to the Head of State in an interview with the media on 2 April, praising the revolutionary vision of Alassane Ouattara whose actions restore the dignity of Ivorian planters ; "Many thanks to the Head of State for the historic decisions he is taking for the happiness of the planters. From 1,800 CFA francs, which was already a good purchase price, he has just decided, for the mid-crop season, to set the purchase price of a kilo of cocoa beans at 2,200 CFA francs. This is unprecedented."

a791.speaker: Siaka Diakité, President of the Onpcc-CI
a791.name: Siaka Diakité
a791.title: President of the Onpcc-CI
a791.speech: Said the organisation is generating enthusiasm among producers and already claims more than 100,000 registered professional producers ; "For us, the first objective of the Onpcc-CI is to obtain legitimacy and the sponsorship of producers, so as to be able to speak legitimately in their name. As for the establishment of the inter-professional body, if our umbrella organisation manages to bring together more than half of Côte d'Ivoire's producers, who number 1,072,000 according to the latest census, we could then consider taking part in the Agricultural Inter-professional Organisation (Oia). For now, our priority remains the legitimisation of the planters."

a791.speaker: Siaka Diakité, President of the Onpcc-CI
a791.name: Siaka Diakité
a791.title: President of the Onpcc-CI
a791.speech: Assures that the purpose of the Onpcc-CI "is to defend producers vis-à-vis the administration and the multinationals, and then to confront the difficulties encountered on the ground" ; "We intend to be present at the negotiating table in order to defend their interests. We are delighted by the trust placed in us by the producers who are joining our organisation en masse. We will do everything not to disappoint them. It is by our work that the producers will judge us."

a796.speaker: Abdullahi Ango, Mandate Secretary, Agriculture and Rural Development Secretariat, FCTA
a796.name: Abdullahi Ango
a796.title: Mandate Secretary, Agriculture and Rural Development Secretariat, FCTA
a796.speech: Disclosed in Abuja, after a week-long meeting with directors, heads of projects and specialised units, that the Secretariat has concluded plans to assess abattoirs, veterinary clinics and farm infrastructure across the territory; also said the facility tours across the area councils would provide the needed platform to engage with farmers, stakeholders and development partners, which he said will help fast-track the implementation of agricultural programmes in the FCT.

a796.speaker: Abdullahi Ango, Mandate Secretary, Agriculture and Rural Development Secretariat, FCTA
a796.name: Abdullahi Ango
a796.title: Mandate Secretary, Agriculture and Rural Development Secretariat, FCTA
a796.speech: Said efforts were ongoing to ensure that farmers received seeds, fertilisers and equipment before the rainy season; he also emphasised the need to equip agricultural extension agents with tools and training, as well as boost public-private partnerships to attract agribusiness investments in the FCT.

a929.speaker: Abeer Etefa, spokesperson for the World Food Programme (WFP)
a929.name: Abeer Etefa
a929.title: spokesperson for the World Food Programme (WFP)
a929.speech: “In the shops, the reserves (of food) amount to a few days, perhaps four or five days” ; reported that the destruction of infrastructure in Gaza, such as the shops where people could collect WFP assistance, hampers the delivery of humanitarian services and that “the shops are facing enormous difficulties in restocking from warehouses” that still have food reserves but are located in the north of the Gaza Strip.

a929.speaker: Abeer Etefa, spokesperson for the World Food Programme (WFP)
a929.name: Abeer Etefa
a929.title: spokesperson for the World Food Programme (WFP)
a929.speech: “I think everyone hopes that we can still get in (at Rafah) and that is why more aid is on the way,” adding that the people who need the assistance are only “a few kilometres away” but “cannot” get into Rafah ; reported that food aid continues to flow towards the region and “is waiting at the border”, adding that a new WFP flight is expected at the end of the day.

a929.speaker: Jens Laerke, spokesperson for the UN Under-Secretary-General in Geneva
a929.name: Jens Laerke
a929.title: spokesperson for the UN Under-Secretary-General in Geneva
a929.speech: Said that Griffiths is due to arrive in Cairo today, and indicated that Griffiths is also due to go to Israel and, “if conditions allow, will travel to the occupied Palestinian territories”, without specifying where.

a980.speaker: East African Legislative Assembly (EALA)
a980.name: East African Legislative Assembly (EALA)
a980.speech: Has passed a resolution urging the EAC Council of Ministers to fast-track the implementation of universal health insurance across all member states to ensure equitable access to quality healthcare.

a980.speaker: Ambassador Ndangiza, EALA Member
a980.name: Ambassador Ndangiza
a980.title: EALA Member
a980.speech: Said the resolution calls on the Council of Ministers and member states to accelerate universal health coverage by allocating at least 15 per cent of their national budgets to the health sector, in line with regional and global development goals. “It is time to find sustainable solutions that reduce dependency on foreign aid and instead prioritise local investment to meet pressing needs, particularly in healthcare. Health must be recognised as a fundamental right for every citizen because health is wealth.”

a980.speaker: Dr Gladbess Salema, EALA Member
a980.name: Dr Gladbess Salema
a980.title: EALA Member
a980.speech: Said that achieving universal health coverage requires more than financial access, it also demands quality service delivery and efficient health systems.

a980.speaker: Kanini Kega, Kenyan legislator
a980.name: Kanini Kega
a980.title: Kenyan legislator
a980.speech: Echoed similar sentiments, observing that recent restrictions on foreign aid have exposed the region’s vulnerabilities; urged EAC nations to strengthen domestic investment and engage the private sector to drive innovation and transformation in healthcare. “Uganda is a good example, having invested 6.1 per cent of its national budget in health, with ongoing efforts to increase funding and achieve self-sufficiency.”

a980.speaker: The Assembly (EALA)
a980.name: The Assembly (EALA)
a980.speech: Commended the EAC Council of Ministers for establishing the East African Health Research Commission (EAHRC) in Burundi, which coordinates research and policy development to improve healthcare across the region; and applauded Rwanda as a model of economic resilience for growing its economy by more than 90 per cent through domestic revenue mobilisation rather than foreign assistance.

a1135.speaker: Sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a1135.name: Sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a1135.speech: Told Reuters that it took a warning of "wasted tax dollars" for a top U.S. official to eventually agree to a deal for the supplies to be used.

a1135.speaker: Two internal USAID memos dated May 5 and May 19 (reviewed by Reuters) and four sources familiar with the matter
a1135.name: Two internal USAID memos dated May 5 and May 19 (reviewed by Reuters) and four sources familiar with the matter
a1135.speech: The deal saved 622 metric tons of the energy-dense biscuits in June, but 496 metric tons, worth $793,000 before they expired this month, will be destroyed.

a1135.speaker: Two sources (anonymous)
a1135.name: Two sources (anonymous)
a1135.speech: Said the wasted biscuits will be turned into landfill or incinerated in the United Arab Emirates.

a1135.speaker: USAID memo of May 5 (verified by three sources)
a1135.name: USAID memo of May 5 (verified by three sources)
a1135.speech: That will cost the U.S. government an additional $100,000.

a1135.speaker: Spokesperson for the State Department
a1135.name: Spokesperson for the State Department
a1135.speech: Confirmed in an email to Reuters that the biscuits would have to be destroyed. But they said the stocks were "purchased as a contingency beyond projections" under the administration of former President Joe Biden, resulting in their expiration.

a1135.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a1135.name: Donald Trump
a1135.title: U.S. President
a1135.speech: Has said the U.S. pays disproportionately for foreign aid, and he wants other countries to shoulder more of the burden.

a1135.speaker: U.N. World Food Programme
a1135.name: U.N. World Food Programme
a1135.speech: Fortified wheat biscuits are calorie-rich and typically deployed in crisis conditions where people lack cooking facilities, "providing immediate nutrition for a child or adult" ; The WFP says 319 million people are facing acute levels of food insecurity worldwide. Of those, 1.9 million people are gripped by catastrophic hunger and on the brink of famine, primarily in Gaza and Sudan.

a1135.speaker: Two sources (anonymous)
a1135.name: Two sources (anonymous)
a1135.speech: Said that after Jeremy Lewin and Kenneth Jackson, operatives of the Department of Government Efficiency, were appointed acting deputy USAID administrators and began terminating food security programmes, USAID staff were barred from communicating with aid organisations that were asking to take the biscuits.

a1135.speaker: A State Department official, speaking on condition of anonymity
a1135.name: A State Department official
a1135.title: speaking on condition of anonymity
a1135.speech: Said it was "entirely false" that USAID staff were barred from communicating with aid groups, and that "there was no direction given … not to engage."

a1135.speaker: Reuters
a1135.name: Reuters
a1135.speech: Reported that a January 25 email sent by Kenneth Jackson emphasizing a "complete halt" to all foreign assistance banned USAID staff from any communications outside of the agency unless approved by their front office.

a1135.speaker: Kenneth Jackson, acting deputy USAID administrator (January 25 memo reviewed by Reuters)
a1135.name: Kenneth Jackson
a1135.title: acting deputy USAID administrator (January 25 memo reviewed by Reuters)
a1135.speech: "Failure to abide by this directive…will result in disciplinary action."

a1135.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a1135.name: Marco Rubio
a1135.title: U.S. Secretary of State
a1135.speech: Told lawmakers on May 21 that no food aid would be wasted, as USAID staff were waiting for Lewin to sign off on a deal to transfer the 622 metric tons of biscuits to the WFP for distribution before they began expiring in September.

a1135.speaker: Five sources familiar with the matter and the May 19 memo
a1135.name: Five sources familiar with the matter and the May 19 memo
a1135.speech: That agreement was approved in June after weeks of waiting.

a1135.speaker: Both sources (anonymous)
a1135.name: Both sources (anonymous)
a1135.speech: Told Reuters that Lewin, who now runs the State Department's Office of Foreign Assistance, did not respond to the request for weeks ; Said it took until early July to begin sending the stocks because generally it requires weeks of work to rearrange shipments after supply chains are disrupted.

a1135.speaker: A State Department official
a1135.name: A State Department official
a1135.speech: Said the memo had to go through revisions and edits before Lewin could sign it on June 2 ; Said Lewin cleared the transfer in a "timely manner," and that consideration had to be given to finding shipping options that were not several times more expensive than the value of the biscuits.

a1135.speaker: USAID staff (memo to Jeremy Lewin)
a1135.name: USAID staff (memo to Jeremy Lewin)
a1135.speech: Warned him that the biscuits had a limited shelf-life and that the agency would have to pay an estimated $125,000 to have them destroyed, resulting in "wasted tax dollars," unless an agreement was struck with WFP to take them.

a1135.speaker: Jeremy Lewin, head of the State Department's Office of Foreign Assistance
a1135.name: Jeremy Lewin
a1135.title: head of the State Department's Office of Foreign Assistance
a1135.speech: Did not respond to requests for comment.

a1135.speaker: A WFP official
a1135.name: A WFP official
a1135.speech: Said it had signed an agreement to receive the biscuits.

a1135.speaker: Reuters analysis using figures from WFP
a1135.name: Reuters analysis using figures from WFP
a1135.speech: The supplies slated for destruction could have fed around 27,000 people for a month.

a1135.speaker: Alexandra Rutishauser-Perera, director of nutrition at Action Against Hunger UK
a1135.name: Alexandra Rutishauser-Perera
a1135.title: director of nutrition at Action Against Hunger UK
a1135.speech: "We knew the suspension of USAID funding would have immediate consequences, and the destruction of emergency food, at a time when acute hunger is at its highest on record, underscores the unintended consequences of such funding cuts."

a1135.speaker: U.S. government data
a1135.name: U.S. government data
a1135.speech: The United States disbursed $61 billion in foreign assistance last year, just over half of it via USAID.

a1135.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State (statement of July 1)
a1135.name: Marco Rubio
a1135.title: U.S. Secretary of State (statement of July 1)
a1135.speech: In a statement on July 1 marking the transfer of USAID to the State Department, Rubio said the U.S. was abandoning what he called a charity-based model and would focus on empowering countries to grow sustainably. "We will favor those nations that have demonstrated both the ability and willingness to help themselves and will target our resources to areas where they can have a multiplier effect and catalyze durable private sector, including American companies, and global investment," he wrote.

a1160.speaker: General Mohamed Hamdane Daglo, leader of Sudan's Rapid Support Forces
a1160.name: General Mohamed Hamdane Daglo
a1160.title: leader of Sudan's Rapid Support Forces
a1160.speech: During his meeting with the Djiboutian president, expressed "his vision for ending the war and reaching a comprehensive solution that will put an end to the suffering of the Sudanese people."

a1160.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of Djibouti and chair of IGAD
a1160.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a1160.title: President of Djibouti and chair of IGAD
a1160.speech: His voice, resonating as an imperious call for an end to hostilities at the last extraordinary IGAD summit, remains engraved in memories — a poignant reminder of the urgent need to silence the guns in the brotherly country of Sudan.

a1160.speaker: United Nations
a1160.name: United Nations
a1160.speech: Warned that nearly nine months of war have plunged Sudan into a downward spiral that is only worsening day by day and that, as the conflict spreads, human suffering worsens, humanitarian access shrinks and hope dwindles ; The United Nations counts human losses amounting to 12,000 souls ; According to the UN, nearly 25 million people will need humanitarian aid in Sudan in 2024.

a1195.speaker: Washington Post (newspaper report)
a1195.name: Washington Post (newspaper report)
a1195.speech: The lead story of the Washington Post on 14 June described a network of clandestine US military bases located across Africa, designed to carry out airborne surveillance of irregular armed groups... The illustrious paper said there are now about a dozen of these pocket-sized bases in Burkina Faso, Uganda, Ethiopia, Djibouti, Kenya and the Seychelles. ; "The nature and extent of the missions, as well as many of the bases being used, have not been previously reported but are partially documented in public Defense Department contracts. The operations have intensified in recent months, part of a growing shadow war against al-Qaeda affiliates and other militant groups."

a1195.speaker: American officials
a1195.name: American officials
a1195.speech: have been pointing to Nigeria's Boko Haram as growing threats to national and regional stability in Africa.

a1195.speaker: General Carter Ham, head of Africom (US Africa Command)
a1195.name: General Carter Ham
a1195.title: head of Africom (US Africa Command)
a1195.speech: In recent testimony to Congress, described American priorities in Africa, saying, "we've prioritised our efforts, focusing on the greatest threats to America, Americans and American interests." ; "Countering the threats posed by al-Qaeda affiliates in East and Northwest Africa remains my number one priority."

a1195.speaker: Africom website (official statement of priorities)
a1195.name: Africom website (official statement of priorities)
a1195.speech: According to Africom's website, the command's top priorities are now: countering terrorism and violent extremist organisations, countering piracy and illicit trafficking, partnering to strengthen defence capabilities, and preparing for and responding to crises.

a1195.speaker: General Carter Ham, head of Africom (US Africa Command)
a1195.name: General Carter Ham
a1195.title: head of Africom (US Africa Command)
a1195.speech: The official view now, as General Ham told Congress several months ago, is: "In Africa, I would say a light footprint is consistent with what we need and consistent with the defence guidance." Ham did allude vaguely to the new, small surveillance bases in his testimony when he added that while not wanting to describe specific locations, the US military hoped to expand its intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance on the continent.

a1195.speaker: Colonel Cyrus Oguna, Kenyan Defence Forces spokesman
a1195.name: Colonel Cyrus Oguna
a1195.title: Kenyan Defence Forces spokesman
a1195.speech: told the Voice of America once the Post story had been published: "As far as we are concerned, (the) US is not using any Kenyan air space or any bases from where they can be able to launch observation vessels. However, I know that we do have bilateral arrangements in terms of sharing information and intelligence to fight terror."

a1195.speaker: American military sources
a1195.name: American military sources
a1195.speech: would confirm to journalists that the US did work "closely with our African partners…to conduct missions or operations that support and further our mutual security goals," they, in turn, offered no details.

a1195.speaker: Washington-based US officials / US embassy in Pretoria / Africom headquarters (non-response)
a1195.name: Washington-based US officials / US embassy in Pretoria / Africom headquarters (non-response)
a1195.speech: news organisations have reported that, throughout Thursday, Washington-based officials were not answering questions about "specific operational details" in the Post's report and the American embassy in Pretoria referred the Daily Maverick to Africom headquarters in Germany. By late Thursday evening, Africom had not responded to queries.

a1195.speaker: Robert Kaplan, "The Coming Anarchy" essay, and CIA Global Trends reports
a1195.name: Robert Kaplan
a1195.title: "The Coming Anarchy" essay, and CIA Global Trends reports
a1195.speech: Much of this thinking drew on the impact of essays like Robert Kaplan's "The Coming Anarchy" or some increasingly ominous Global Trends reports issued by the CIA. These writings described a world – and most especially an Africa – increasingly afflicted by global pandemics, cyber-crime activities, trans-national terrorism, relentless climate change and resulting forced population migrations.

a1195.speaker: US embassy cables released through WikiLeaks
a1195.name: US embassy cables released through WikiLeaks
a1195.speech: According to cables released through WikiLeaks, this influx of military personnel sometimes gave the US embassy a kind of bureaucratic dyspepsia.

a1195.speaker: Steve McDonald, Africa-watcher at the Wilson Center in Washington
a1195.name: Steve McDonald
a1195.title: Africa-watcher at the Wilson Center in Washington
a1195.speech: predicts warily "Whatever the justification for military purposes - like chasing the LRA, which we all find laudable - the perception among Africans will be very negative, just as when Africom was announced by Bush in September 2007. I am sure there will have been clearances with governments, like Burkina Faso, Liberia, Ethiopia, Kenya, and others who would welcome this presence's economic spin-offs, but the revelation will cause widespread popular discontent…or staunch the perception of a militarisation of our policy, that started with Africom."

a1195.speaker: Scott Firsing, US-Africa military relations and terrorism expert based in South Africa
a1195.name: Scott Firsing
a1195.title: US-Africa military relations and terrorism expert based in South Africa
a1195.speech: calls the efforts depicted in the Post story a welcome development. Firsing says: "Surveillance and intelligence-gathering operations are always a welcome and necessary first move, and I am glad to learn this has been taking place for some time now. Nevertheless, once that threat is understood, the next logical step is to eliminate it by the US supporting African militaries on the ground or in the air."

a1252.speaker: Evelyn Anite, Uganda Investment State Minister
a1252.name: Evelyn Anite
a1252.title: Uganda Investment State Minister
a1252.speech: During a visit to a state-of-the-art exhibition centre set to be unveiled this weekend for Ugandans looking to explore business opportunities, highlighted how power solutions firm Chint, once dependent on imported finished goods, is now manufacturing prepaid meters, cables, and soon LED lights right here in Kampala.

a1561.speaker: African Tax Administration [Forum] (cited)
a1561.name: African Tax Administration [Forum] (cited)
a1561.speech: Cited as the source for the finding that rising debt levels and projected double-digit declines in official development assistance have highlighted the dire need for action plans that will enable Africa to pay for its own development; Africa needs $1.6 trillion to achieve its Sustainable Development Goals by 2030, translating into additional funding requirements of $194 billion per annum.

a1591.speaker: Wang Yi, member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs of China
a1591.name: Wang Yi
a1591.title: member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs of China
a1591.speech: said in his speech that since the beginning of the new era, President Xi Jinping has repeatedly put forward proposals for resolving the Palestinian issue, and has contributed Chinese wisdom and solutions to the settlement of the Palestinian issue; that this is an important historic moment in the cause of Palestinian liberation, when 14 Palestinian factions gather in Beijing in the spirit of national righteousness; that the Chinese side appreciates the efforts made by all parties to reconcile and congratulates the successful Beijing dialogue and the signing of the Beijing Declaration.

a1591.speaker: Wang Yi, member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs of China
a1591.name: Wang Yi
a1591.title: member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs of China
a1591.speech: pointed out that only when all Palestinian factions speak with one voice can the voice of justice be louder, and only by joining hands and advancing side by side can the cause of national liberation succeed; that the most important consensus reached at the Beijing dialogue is to achieve great reconciliation and unity among the 14 factions, the core result is to make it clear that the PLO is the sole legitimate representative of all the Palestinian people, the most prominent highlight is the agreement to form an interim national reconciliation government around the post-war governance of Gaza, and the strongest call is to realize the true independent state of Palestine in accordance with the relevant United Nations resolutions; that the key to internal reconciliation is to strengthen confidence, grasp the direction and proceed in an orderly and gradual manner; that reconciliation is an internal affair for all Palestinian factions and cannot be separated from the support of the international community, and that China and the vast number of Arab and Islamic countries share the same direction and goal.

a1591.speaker: Wang Yi, member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs of China
a1591.name: Wang Yi
a1591.title: member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs of China
a1591.speech: said that the Palestinian issue is the core of the Middle East issue; that China has never had any selfish interests on the question of Palestine and was one of the first countries to recognize the Palestine Liberation Organization and the State of Palestine; "What we value is morality, and what we advocate is justice"; and proposed a "three-step approach": first, to promote a comprehensive, durable and sustainable ceasefire in the Gaza Strip as soon as possible and to ensure humanitarian assistance and access; second, to uphold the principle of "Palestinians governing Palestine" and work together to promote post-war governance in Gaza, with the international community supporting the Palestinian factions in forming an interim Government of National Consensus; third, to promote Palestine as a full Member of the United Nations and to begin the implementation of the two-State solution, supporting the convening of a larger, more authoritative and more effective international peace conference with a timetable and road map.

a1591.speaker: Wang Yi, member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs of China
a1591.name: Wang Yi
a1591.title: member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs of China
a1591.speech: said that the realization of internal reconciliation in Palestine will bring hope and a future to the Palestinian people, and is also an important step in promoting the settlement of the Palestinian issue and achieving peace and stability in the Middle East; that China sincerely hopes all Palestinian factions will achieve an independent Palestinian state on the basis of internal reconciliation at an early date, and is ready to strengthen communication and coordination with all parties concerned and make joint efforts to implement the Beijing Declaration reached that day.

a1591.speaker: Alul, head of the Fatah delegation, and Moussa, head of the Hamas delegation
a1591.name: Alul
a1591.title: head of the Fatah delegation, and Moussa, head of the Hamas delegation
a1591.speech: delivered speeches on behalf of all Palestinian factions, emphasizing that China has a special and important position in the minds of the Palestinian people, and sincerely thanked President Xi Jinping and China for their long-term unwavering support and selfless assistance to Palestine; highly appreciated China's commitment as a major country upholding justice for Palestine in the international community, and expressed deep gratitude to China for its strong support for intra-Palestinian reconciliation and dialogue.

a1677.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Chief Executive Officer of Standard Bank Malawi
a1677.name: Phillip Madinga
a1677.title: Chief Executive Officer of Standard Bank Malawi
a1677.speech: Said in a statement: "We welcome the new administration's resolve for a return to economic stability, predictability and strong governance." ; "The bank looks forward to partnering with government and other key stakeholders to support President Mutharika's plan to immediately tackle prevailing macroeconomic challenges."

a1677.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Chief Executive Officer of Standard Bank Malawi
a1677.name: Phillip Madinga
a1677.title: Chief Executive Officer of Standard Bank Malawi
a1677.speech: Said that attracting foreign direct investment from major economies such as the United States and China, as outlined in the president's inauguration speech, would be critical to unlocking Malawi's growth potential and achieving meaningful economic recovery.

a1677.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Chief Executive Officer of Standard Bank Malawi
a1677.name: Phillip Madinga
a1677.title: Chief Executive Officer of Standard Bank Malawi
a1677.speech: Noted the president's intention to renew relations with Washington through his personal ties with U.S. President Donald Trump: "Easing diplomatic hurdles with the U.S. should set the stage for dialogue aimed at finding solutions for Malawi's economy, trade and diplomatic relations," adding that the loss of development and technical support following USAID's departure called for renewed engagement.

a1677.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Chief Executive Officer of Standard Bank Malawi
a1677.name: Phillip Madinga
a1677.title: Chief Executive Officer of Standard Bank Malawi
a1677.speech: Said the bank expected stronger cooperation between the private and public sectors during the government's three-month transition period: "The stage should be prepared for a reset of Malawi's economic trajectory where the resolve to return to stability through fiscal discipline, good governance, dialogue with donors and creditors, and improved trade relations is unambiguous."

a2001.speaker: Abdirahman Yusuf, Somali immigrant and founder of the Somali Development Center (SDC)
a2001.name: Abdirahman Yusuf
a2001.title: Somali immigrant and founder of the Somali Development Center (SDC)
a2001.speech: spoke out against Trump’s travel ban that targeted predominantly Muslim countries during President-elect Donald Trump’s first presidency.

a2001.speaker: Abdirahman Yusuf, founder of the Somali Development Center (SDC)
a2001.name: Abdirahman Yusuf
a2001.title: founder of the Somali Development Center (SDC)
a2001.speech: on why SDC was founded and what it does: “Because of the challenges of language, religion and racial issues, we thought it was absolutely necessary to establish an organization that could work with these people” ; “We wanted to help them assimilate and succeed and integrate into society so they have a better life than the one they left” ; “Right now you can imagine it, no one can get everything done in three months, so folks need to go to other sources for support.”

a2001.speaker: Abdirahman Yusuf, founder of the Somali Development Center (SDC)
a2001.name: Abdirahman Yusuf
a2001.title: founder of the Somali Development Center (SDC)
a2001.speech: emphasized that anyone is welcome at SDC: “Monday to Friday, the doors are open here for people to walk in — our clientele from East Africa, North Africa, West Africa, Afghanistan, Ukraine, Hispanic folks, you name it” ; “Anyone who’s a refugee or immigrant and needs assistance walks in and we help them when we can, and if we cannot, then we connect them to the right place.”

a2001.speaker: Abdirahman Yusuf, founder of the Somali Development Center (SDC)
a2001.name: Abdirahman Yusuf
a2001.title: founder of the Somali Development Center (SDC)
a2001.speech: on the challenges facing immigrants and the organisation: “It’s like starting anew in a completely new country, new culture, new language, new everything, and that’s their challenge. Our challenge is lack of resources, enough manpower or people who know how to do these things, who can understand the folks to deliver [these] services and help people move into more stable lives.”

a2001.speaker: Said Ahmed, CEO of the non-profit United Somali Youth and former SDC participant
a2001.name: Said Ahmed
a2001.title: CEO of the non-profit United Somali Youth and former SDC participant
a2001.speech: feels the group’s support was foundational to his ability to land on his feet and ultimately found a youth sports program, earn a PhD, teach at Harvard and run for City Council in Boston’s 7th district; SDC was a place where he belonged, and it bolstered him.

a2001.speaker: Colleen Leddie, program director at SDC
a2001.name: Colleen Leddie
a2001.title: program director at SDC
a2001.speech: says that watching the hard work it took her grandparents to find success and establish themselves has inspired her to help others do the same.

a2001.speaker: Munira Farah, health services coordinator at SDC
a2001.name: Munira Farah
a2001.title: health services coordinator at SDC
a2001.speech: “Meeting the needs of people is really important to me” ; “Learning about people every day and seeing different personalities really inspires me to do the work that I do” ; on reuniting a family separated for four years: “I’m pretty proud of myself that I’m the reason why someone’s family is here” ; on language: “They have to learn English or they can’t get anywhere” ; “We were instrumental in hiring bilingual Somali-certified teachers from all over the world.”

a2001.speaker: Abdillahi Abdirahman, owner of Butterfly Falafel and former SDC board member
a2001.name: Abdillahi Abdirahman
a2001.title: owner of Butterfly Falafel and former SDC board member
a2001.speech: “These people come from the border—they’re looking for a safe place, they’re looking for a better life, which they can get here” ; “The people who are complaining, if they [are] not an immigrant, their parents are immigrants or their grandparents are immigrants, they just have to know that” ; “If you look at Roxbury, there’s a lot of Somali businesses, that’s changed — it changed for the better, and the community culturally and politically has diversified. That’s what immigrants will do, everywhere they go, everywhere they come from” ; “At the end of the day, we are obligated to help strangers. We have to show them sympathy and kindness. We have to welcome strangers — it doesn’t matter what color.”

a2048.speaker: SowetanLIVE (South African news site)
a2048.name: SowetanLIVE (South African news site)
a2048.speech: He was accused of firing between 14 and 15 live rounds on a stage in front of 20,000 EFF supporters, according to South African news site SowetanLIVE.

a2048.speaker: Julius Malema, leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2048.name: Julius Malema
a2048.title: leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2048.speech: In his defence, told the court the firearm was not his and that he had fired the shots to rouse the crowd.

a2048.speaker: Twanet Olivier, magistrate (court ruling)
a2048.name: Twanet Olivier
a2048.title: magistrate (court ruling)
a2048.speech: It took three days for magistrate Twanet Olivier to tell Malema "you are found guilty as charged". The case was postponed to January 2026 for pre-sentencing.

a2048.speaker: Julius Malema, leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2048.name: Julius Malema
a2048.title: leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2048.speech: Told supporters that "going to prison or death is a badge of honour" ; "We cannot be scared of prison [or] to die for the revolution. Whatever they want to do, they must know we will never retreat," he said outside the East London regional court ; vowed to challenge the judgment, even up to South Africa's highest court, the Constitutional Court.

a2048.speaker: Julius Malema, leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2048.name: Julius Malema
a2048.title: leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2048.speech: After an incident where a white man allegedly assaulted an EFF member, said: "No white man is going to beat me up… you must never be scared to kill. A revolution demands that at some point there must be killing." ; has called for the seizure of white-owned land and argues that more should be done to transfer wealth to the black majority.

a2048.speaker: South Africa's equality court (ruling)
a2048.name: South Africa's equality court (ruling)
a2048.speech: Ruled that these remarks "demonstrated an intent to incite harm".

a2048.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2048.name: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2048.speech: Said the remarks were taken out of context.

a2048.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2048.name: Donald Trump
a2048.title: US President
a2048.speech: Showed a video of the radical leader during his heated meeting with South African President Cyril Ramaphosa in the White House in May, using it as part of his "evidence" that genocide was being committed against white Afrikaners in South Africa.

a2048.speaker: UK Home Office
a2048.name: UK Home Office
a2048.speech: Said he had been deemed "non-conducive to the public good".

a2062.speaker: Nelson Mandela, 1918-2013 (quoted)
a2062.name: Nelson Mandela
a2062.title: 1918-2013 (quoted)
a2062.speech: “A country is measured by the way it treats its children.”

a2062.speaker: News Report, August 19, 2025 (cited)
a2062.name: News Report
a2062.title: August 19, 2025 (cited)
a2062.speech: “Crisis alert: UNICEF seeks lifesaving N240bn for Nigeria aid projects.”

a2062.speaker: Emile Zola, 1840-1902 (quoted)
a2062.name: Emile Zola
a2062.title: 1840-1902 (quoted)
a2062.speech: “If you shut up the truth and bury it underground, it will but grow and gather itself such explosive power that, the day it busts through, it will blow up everything in its way.”

a2062.speaker: Francis Butichi, UNICEF Chief of Maiduguri Field Office
a2062.name: Francis Butichi
a2062.title: UNICEF Chief of Maiduguri Field Office
a2062.speech: “We are all aware of the global funding cut that has threatened humanitarian operations across the world. The impact is profoundly crushing at the local level, where conflict, climate change and disease are recurrent.”

a2062.speaker: Lee Kuan Yew, 1923-2015 (quoted)
a2062.name: Lee Kuan Yew
a2062.title: 1923-2015 (quoted)
a2062.speech: “When those in office regard the power vested in them as personal prerogative, they enrich themselves, promote their families and favour their friends…”

a2062.speaker: A recent report (cited)
a2062.name: A recent report (cited)
a2062.speech: Informed Nigerians that a few state Governors spent N1.3 trillion on renovation of Governors' Mansions and close to N100bn on foreign trips in search of elusive Foreign Direct Investment, FDI, and returned home empty-handed.

a2062.speaker: Bismarck Rewane, financial analyst
a2062.name: Bismarck Rewane
a2062.title: financial analyst
a2062.speech: Recently pointed to the monumental waste of public funds by states embarking on airport projects – which perennially lose money.

a2062.speaker: Mahatma Gandhi, 1869-1948 (quoted)
a2062.name: Mahatma Gandhi
a2062.title: 1869-1948 (quoted)
a2062.speech: “There are people in the world, so hungry, that God cannot appear to them except in form of bread.”

a2230.speaker: US draft resolution to the UN General Assembly (document)
a2230.name: US draft resolution to the UN General Assembly (document)
a2230.speech: Seen by AFP on Friday and only 65 words long, it calls for "a swift end to the conflict and calls for a lasting peace between Ukraine and Russia", and does not mention respect for Ukraine's territorial integrity.

a2230.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a2230.name: Marco Rubio
a2230.title: US Secretary of State
a2230.speech: Urged in a statement the UN member countries to approve this "simple" and "historic" new resolution and "all member states to support it, in order to chart a path towards peace."

a2230.speaker: Vassily Nebenzia, Russian Ambassador to the UN
a2230.name: Vassily Nebenzia
a2230.title: Russian Ambassador to the UN
a2230.speech: Commented that the resolution "is a good idea", while regretting the absence of any reference "to the roots" of the conflict.

a2230.speaker: Nicolas de Rivière, French Ambassador to the UN
a2230.name: Nicolas de Rivière
a2230.title: French Ambassador to the UN

a2230.speaker: Richard Gowan, International Crisis Group
a2230.name: Richard Gowan
a2230.title: International Crisis Group
a2230.speech: Told AFP: "A minimalist text (...) that does not condemn Russian aggression or refer explicitly to Ukraine's territorial integrity looks like a betrayal of Kyiv and a low blow against the EU, but also contempt for the principles at the heart of international law."

a2230.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2230.name: Donald Trump
a2230.title: US President
a2230.speech: Said Volodymyr Zelensky and Vladimir Putin were going to "have to talk to each other", to "end the massacre of millions of people", but judged that the Ukrainian's presence was "not important" at negotiations with Russia ; "I've had very good discussions with Putin, and I've had discussions that were not as good with Ukraine. They have no cards in hand, but they play it tough." ; "We are not going to let this continue." ; "It's been three years that (Volodymyr Zelensky) has been in meetings and nothing has been done", he said in an interview with Fox Radio, "So I don't think he is very important to take part in meetings."

a2230.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2230.name: Donald Trump
a2230.title: US President
a2230.speech: Refused to blame Moscow for the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, saying Western leaders "should not have let her attack."

a2230.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2230.name: Donald Trump
a2230.title: US President
a2230.speech: Targeted French President Emmanuel Macron and British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who he said have done "nothing" to end the war.

a2230.speaker: Donald Trump and his aides
a2230.name: Donald Trump and his aides
a2230.speech: Judged "unrealistic" Ukraine's accession to NATO and its ambition to retake the territories it has lost to Russia.

a2230.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2230.name: Donald Trump
a2230.title: US President
a2230.speech: In early February had announced that he wanted to obtain access to 50% of Ukraine's strategic minerals in exchange for the American aid already delivered.

a2230.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a2230.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a2230.title: Ukrainian President
a2230.speech: Wants an agreement on US access to Ukraine's strategic minerals that is "fair" ; explained in a video message broadcast on social media on Friday evening that Ukraine and the United States were working "on a draft agreement" concerning minerals ; had angrily rejected the first version of an agreement, stressing that his country was "not for sale", and had repeated his proposal to negotiate American "investments" in exchange for "security guarantees" against Russia.

a2230.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a2230.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a2230.title: Ukrainian President
a2230.speech: Had said he had "productive" exchanges with Keith Kellogg.

a2230.speaker: Keith Kellogg, envoy of the US President to Ukraine
a2230.name: Keith Kellogg
a2230.title: envoy of the US President to Ukraine
a2230.speech: Had described Zelensky as a "courageous and besieged leader of a nation at war."

a2230.speaker: Dmitry Peskov, Kremlin spokesman
a2230.name: Dmitry Peskov
a2230.title: Kremlin spokesman
a2230.speech: Reaffirmed on Friday that President Vladimir Putin was "open" to peace talks.

a2230.speaker: Russia (official demands)
a2230.name: Russia (official demands)
a2230.speech: Demands in particular that Kyiv cede four Ukrainian regions in addition to Crimea, annexed in 2014, and that Ukraine never join NATO.

a2230.speaker: Draft resolution prepared by Ukraine and the Europeans (document)
a2230.name: Draft resolution prepared by Ukraine and the Europeans (document)
a2230.speech: Stresses the need to "redouble" diplomatic efforts to end the war "this year", takes note of the initiatives of several member states that have presented "their vision for a comprehensive and lasting peace agreement", and repeats the General Assembly's previous demands for an immediate and unconditional withdrawal of Russian troops from Ukraine and the cessation of Russia's attacks against Ukraine.

a2230.speaker: Russian army
a2230.name: Russian army
a2230.speech: Again claimed on Friday the capture of two localities in eastern Ukraine.

a2314.speaker: Raphael Morav, Ambassador of Israel to Ethiopia
a2314.name: Raphael Morav
a2314.title: Ambassador of Israel to Ethiopia
a2314.speech: said that violence starts with words and then it becomes acts of violence that may end in genocides and other horrible acts, while talking about the liberation of the Auschwitz camp: "It was the International Day for the commemoration of the victims of the Holocaust. Although it is 75 years since the Auschwitz extermination camp was liberated, the issue of Holocaust is still very relevant today... The most important lesson of the holocaust is that violence starts with words; therefore, when we hear discourses of racist attitudes and heinous speeches of hatred and anti-Semitism, bigotry and such negative things, we have to be vigilant." ; "The world stood still 75 years ago when the Holocaust took place, and we thought it would never happen again, yet we regretfully saw several genocides in the world in Cambodia in the 70s and in Rwanda 25 years ago, so it means that it can still happen. Therefore, we need to be vigilant and act beforehand." ; "I am a strong believer in education... So I think education is the key to prevent future acts of this kind. At the same time, politically speaking, when we hear discourse of hatred and anti-Semitism, bigotry we need to take action, to say this will not continue, we will not allow such expression to be tolerated."

a2314.speaker: Raphael Morav, Ambassador of Israel to Ethiopia
a2314.name: Raphael Morav
a2314.title: Ambassador of Israel to Ethiopia
a2314.speech: on reports that trips to Ethiopia for Israeli students had been suspended: "It’s rather wrong information that I saw on the press. It was suggesting that the Ministry of Education of Israel is suspending trips of students from Israel to Ethiopia and this is incorrect. What is true is that there is a travel advisory to Ethiopia that calls for Israeli citizens to refrain from unnecessary trips to the Somali region and the Somali region only. That is due to a potential threat of Al-Shabaab terrorist activities against Israeli nationals... On the contrary, we encourage Israelis to visit Ethiopia, invest in the country and make business with Ethiopians partners." ; "Next Monday, I am receiving 35 youths who are coming to Ethiopia from Israel. We call it a 'Roots Trip' because they will be in the footsteps of the Beta Israel heritage."

a2314.speaker: Raphael Morav, Ambassador of Israel to Ethiopia
a2314.name: Raphael Morav
a2314.title: Ambassador of Israel to Ethiopia
a2314.speech: "Israeli investments in Ethiopia are mainly in the agricultural sector; normally many of them are private farms that have developed new varieties in Ethiopia. For example, one farm has introduced strawberries in Ethiopia... Today it’s a huge exporter of strawberries from Ethiopia to all over the world. We have another Israeli farm, which is growing chives, it is one of the biggest producer of chives in the world... This is the type of investment we are encouraging because they contribute not only to the economy of Ethiopia in terms of employment and transformation of agriculture but as well as they are all important exporters who are also bringing hard currency to Ethiopia." ; "Beyond investment, it’s worth mentioning that the biggest drip irrigation project in the world is in Ethiopia conducted by an Israeli company Netafim... The project is about irrigation of 7000 hectares in the Wolkaite area for sugar cane... It’s a big operation worth over $200 million."

a2314.speaker: Raphael Morav, Ambassador of Israel to Ethiopia
a2314.name: Raphael Morav
a2314.title: Ambassador of Israel to Ethiopia
a2314.speech: "We have a very important project of cooperation in development with the Ministry of Agriculture and USAID that has been running for 13 years, for the introduction of high quality varieties of avocado. Today, thanks to this project, Ethiopia is an exporter of avocado fruits to Europe..." ; "We have set up six nurseries for avocado seedlings in Ethiopia that are producing over half a million seedlings per year and in addition to that, thanks to our encouragement, the private sector is now entering this activity and already produces about half a million more seedlings... It is really making a transformation in the agricultural sector of Ethiopia because it became the most profitable crop in Ethiopia, more than coffee or sesame or any other traditional crop."

a2314.speaker: Raphael Morav, Ambassador of Israel to Ethiopia
a2314.name: Raphael Morav
a2314.title: Ambassador of Israel to Ethiopia
a2314.speech: "There has been a Jewish presence in Ethiopia for about 2000 years and the Jews lived very closely with their Christian and Muslim neighbors, mostly in good relations... They left Ethiopia 30-40 years ago, however Ethiopia has not left them and remains in their heart." ; "An Israeli organization \"Matasabia\" (remembrance) decided to restore all the places of the Beta Israel heritage in Ethiopia... their initiative is to create a \"Beta Israel trail\" that will present and preserve the heritage sites of Beta Israel." ; "The first thing that they decided to do is to restore an old and important Jewish cemetery in Dabat area in the Amhara region... The good surprise was that the authorities that were there, the governor of the region, the mayor and other authorities all say that this is also part of Ethiopia’s heritage; it’s not just Beta Israel."

a2314.speaker: Raphael Morav, Ambassador of Israel to Ethiopia
a2314.name: Raphael Morav
a2314.title: Ambassador of Israel to Ethiopia
a2314.speech: "As a conclusion of what we have said, I would say the relations are very good, maybe even excellent. We are aiming higher and there is space to deepen and reinforce the relations. Politically speaking we had the exchange of visits at the highest level. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed visited Israel in September, the President of the State of Israel visited in May 2018, the Prime Minister of Israel visited in 2016..." ; "These political relations are translated into good economic relations; we are encouraging and working to bring more investment from Israel to Ethiopia... Last but not least, we are excited that Ethiopia will have, for the first time, free and fair democratic elections. We are supportive of this process of political reforms as well as the economic and social ones. I am convinced the future is even more promising."

a2337.speaker: Edgar Chibaka, serial entrepreneur, investor and Chairperson of the UK Malawi Chamber of Commerce (opinion author)
a2337.name: Edgar Chibaka
a2337.title: serial entrepreneur, investor and Chairperson of the UK Malawi Chamber of Commerce (opinion author)
a2337.speech: Argues that Trump's USAID cuts and the IMF's withdrawal of its Extended Credit Facility should be seen "not as a catastrophe, but as a long-overdue opportunity—an invitation to reclaim our national dignity, reshape our identity, and forge our own destiny" ; "Trump's USAID cuts and the IMF's exit may feel like abandonment to some, but for Malawi, they may be the wake-up call we needed." ; "We must move from aid to trade, from foreign dependency to local ownership, from political rhetoric to economic action."

a2337.speaker: Edgar Chibaka, serial entrepreneur, investor and Chairperson of the UK Malawi Chamber of Commerce (opinion author)
a2337.name: Edgar Chibaka
a2337.title: serial entrepreneur, investor and Chairperson of the UK Malawi Chamber of Commerce (opinion author)
a2337.speech: Writes that under President Bakili Muluzi in the early 1990s Malawi became a testing ground for structural adjustment programs dictated by the IMF and World Bank, which "proved catastrophic for ordinary Malawians" ; describes a "consultant economy" in which international consultants are "paid handsomely to offer advice on problems they neither fully understand nor experience firsthand" and argues that donor institutions insisting Malawians think and act like them "are not empowering us. They are erasing us."

a2337.speaker: Edgar Chibaka, serial entrepreneur, investor and Chairperson of the UK Malawi Chamber of Commerce (opinion author)
a2337.name: Edgar Chibaka
a2337.title: serial entrepreneur, investor and Chairperson of the UK Malawi Chamber of Commerce (opinion author)
a2337.speech: Argues Malawi's journey to self-reliance will remain a pipe dream without confronting corruption that has enabled foreign business cartels, particularly within parts of the Asian community, to dominate and exploit the economy ; "These are not development partners. They are economic saboteurs masquerading as investors."

a2361.speaker: International Organisation for Migration
a2361.name: International Organisation for Migration
a2361.speech: According to it, more than two million people remain internally displaced across Nigeria north-east.

a2361.speaker: National Bureau of Statistics (2023 survey)
a2361.name: National Bureau of Statistics (2023 survey)
a2361.speech: Identified 340 Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) camps across seven northern states.

a2361.speaker: Solomon Folorunsho, pastor and leader of the Home for the Needy IDP Camp
a2361.name: Solomon Folorunsho
a2361.title: pastor and leader of the Home for the Needy IDP Camp
a2361.speech: Told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN): "I was moved by the overwhelming spate of child neglect and insurgency." ; "I only wanted to give these children a ray of hope. Seeing them graduate as doctors, lawyers, and engineers is proof that God is faithful."

a2361.speaker: Solomon Folorunsho, pastor and leader of the Home for the Needy IDP Camp
a2361.name: Solomon Folorunsho
a2361.title: pastor and leader of the Home for the Needy IDP Camp
a2361.speech: Stated that the foundation takes great care not to admit criminals or individuals of questionable character into the camp: "We carry out background checks using information from relatives and traditional leaders in the home states of the displaced persons. Often, we also seek the assistance of security agencies to ensure that those we admit are genuinely displaced and not persons with dubious backgrounds." ; added that although many of the IDPs are of school age, the foundation conducts examinations and interviews to determine the appropriate class placement, and that "Those who are either above school age or educationally disadvantaged are guided to choose a vocational training programme that suits their interests."

a2361.speaker: Solomon Folorunsho, pastor and leader of the Home for the Needy IDP Camp
a2361.name: Solomon Folorunsho
a2361.title: pastor and leader of the Home for the Needy IDP Camp
a2361.speech: Told NAN that no fewer than 147 survivors in the camp recently completed the Senior Secondary School Examination: "We were able to register 147 of our children in the just concluded NECO and NABTEB examinations. 140 out of the 147 sat for the Joint Admission Matriculation Board (JAMB) examination, and they did very well, as one person scored above 300 and more than 123 scored above 200. However, we are expecting admission for about 145 of them, taking into cognisance the released cut-off mark for admission into tertiary institutions by JAMB some time ago." ; also told NAN that six of the survivors were currently undergoing the mandatory National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) programme, while five were recently called to the Nigerian Bar.

a2361.speaker: Solomon Folorunsho, pastor and leader of the Home for the Needy IDP Camp
a2361.name: Solomon Folorunsho
a2361.title: pastor and leader of the Home for the Needy IDP Camp
a2361.speech: Said: "Every child on the street has the potential to be a doctor, lawyer, or innovator. If you support that child, you could be saving the world from future vices."

a2361.speaker: Evelyn Omigie, supervisor at the Home for the Needy camp
a2361.name: Evelyn Omigie
a2361.title: supervisor at the Home for the Needy camp
a2361.speech: Noted that the home had produced no fewer than 85 graduates across medicine, pharmacy, law, and other disciplines: "Recent years alone have seen five medical doctors, several pharmacists, dozens of accountants, and multiple lawyers."

a2361.speaker: Evelyn Omigie, supervisor at the Home for the Needy camp
a2361.name: Evelyn Omigie
a2361.title: supervisor at the Home for the Needy camp
a2361.speech: Spoke of Amos Ishaku, a former resident who graduated from Edo State University, Uzairue with a First Class degree in Chemical Engineering in November 2023: "He achieved a remarkable Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 4.80, making him the best graduating student in the Faculty of Engineering. His academic excellence earned him several accolades, including the Mike Ozekhome Award for the overall best graduating student and the Best Student awards in both the Department of Chemical Engineering and the Faculty of Engineering. Additionally, Ishaku was honoured with a 2.5 million naira Entrepreneurship Award for his outstanding business proposal during his time at the university. In August 2024, he secured a fully funded PhD scholarship at the University of Illinois, Chicago, US, marking a significant milestone in his academic journey."

a2361.speaker: Ayuba Philemon, camp resident and Law student at Western Delta University
a2361.name: Ayuba Philemon
a2361.title: camp resident and Law student at Western Delta University
a2361.speech: Said: "I thought I would never see a classroom again. But at the camp, I found safety, education, and purpose. From Christlike Primary School through to university, everything was made possible by the Home for the Needy."

a2361.speaker: Blessing Moses, camp resident and nurse displaced from Mubi North in 2015
a2361.name: Blessing Moses
a2361.title: camp resident and nurse displaced from Mubi North in 2015
a2361.speech: Recalled: "I enrolled in school immediately after arriving. Today, I am a qualified nurse. Giving back through the clinic is my way of saying thank you."

a2361.speaker: Obadiah Philemon, camp resident and Accountancy graduate of the University of Benin
a2361.name: Obadiah Philemon
a2361.title: camp resident and Accountancy graduate of the University of Benin
a2361.speech: Said: "There were times when learning meant sitting under trees. But this camp gave me a second chance. Now, I help the next generation find theirs."

a2361.speaker: Naomi Ehigie, leader of the Kindness Family
a2361.name: Naomi Ehigie
a2361.title: leader of the Kindness Family
a2361.speech: Said: "We first visited through the Jesus Fellowship Prayer Band, and I was deeply touched. We built a kitchen in 2017, donated utensils, and still provide food and supplies. Every child here deserves a chance."

a2559.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (official communique)
a2559.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (official communique)
a2559.speech: Reported that the Council of Ministers met in ordinary session on Wednesday 23 April 2014 in Porto-Novo under the chairmanship of the President of the Republic, Head of State, Head of Government, and that at the beginning of the session the Head of State observed a minute of silence in memory of the late Yvette Angele Felicite Titus (Daizo), Daate Mante Tchoropa, Ignacio Koladjo Odoubourou, Daniel Nagnonhou and Barthelemy Nato.

a2559.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (official communique)
a2559.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (official communique)
a2559.speech: Stated that during the session the Council adopted several draft decrees, including decrees ending the secondment to the Constitutional Court of magistrates Clemence Yimbere (Dansou) and Clotilde Medegan (Nougbode); a decree creating the Office for the Management of World Food Programme Projects (OGP-PAM) and approving its statutes; a decree creating revenue-collection offices in the communes of Karimama, Lalo and Agbangnizoun; a decree setting the conditions for the 2013-2014 cashew nut marketing campaign; a decree creating the National Institute for Training Engineering and Capacity Building of Trainers (INIFRCF); a decree amending decree no. 2010-021 on the National Commission for Information Technology and Liberties; a decree on implementing law no. 2012-36 on the Beninese Human Rights Commission; and the implementing decrees for law no. 2013-06 of 25 November 2013 establishing the electoral code.

a2559.speaker: Minister of Economy and Finance of Benin (communication to the Council of Ministers)
a2559.name: Minister of Economy and Finance of Benin (communication to the Council of Ministers)
a2559.speech: Presented a communication on the state of implementation of the decisions of the Council of Ministers for the first half of 2013.

a2559.speaker: Minister of Health of Benin (communication to the Council of Ministers)
a2559.name: Minister of Health of Benin (communication to the Council of Ministers)
a2559.speech: Presented a communication on the payment of Benin's arrears of contributions to the African Public Health Emergency Fund for the 2012-2013 biennium.

a2559.speaker: Minister of the Interior, Public Security and Religious Affairs of Benin (report)
a2559.name: Minister of the Interior
a2559.title: Public Security and Religious Affairs of Benin (report)
a2559.speech: Reported on the 37th session of the joint Benin-Togo border commission, held in Bassila, Ouake, Savalou, Djidja and Djakotomey from 3 to 5 February 2014.

a2559.speaker: Minister of Decentralisation, Local Governance, Administration and Territorial Planning of Benin (report)
a2559.name: Minister of Decentralisation
a2559.title: Local Governance, Administration and Territorial Planning of Benin (report)
a2559.speech: Reported on the operation to have the national budget take over the salaries of the communications staff of the former urban districts and sub-prefectures.

a2559.speaker: Minister of Development, Economic Analysis and Forecasting and Minister of Industry, Trade and Small and Medium Enterprises of Benin (joint report)
a2559.name: Minister of Development
a2559.title: Economic Analysis and Forecasting and Minister of Industry, Trade and Small and Medium Enterprises of Benin (joint report)
a2559.speech: Reported jointly on the 12th AGOA forum, held in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, from 9 to 13 August 2013.

a2559.speaker: Minister of Economy and Finance and Minister of Energy, Petroleum and Mineral Research, Water and Renewable Energy Development of Benin (joint report)
a2559.name: Minister of Economy and Finance and Minister of Energy
a2559.title: Petroleum and Mineral Research, Water and Renewable Energy Development of Benin (joint report)
a2559.speech: Reported jointly on the official visit of a delegation of the Ministers in charge of Finance and Energy to China from 18 to 25 November 2013 in the framework of negotiations for the financing and execution of the Adjaralla hydroelectric development works on the Mono River.

a2559.speaker: Minister of Labour, Public Service, Administrative and Institutional Reform, in charge of Social Dialogue, of Benin (report)
a2559.name: Minister of Labour
a2559.title: Public Service, Administrative and Institutional Reform, in charge of Social Dialogue, of Benin (report)
a2559.speech: Reported on the proceedings of the first extraordinary session of the National Labour Council (CNT) on raising the Guaranteed Interprofessional Minimum Wage (SMIG).

a2559.speaker: Minister of Urban Planning, Housing and Sanitation of Benin (report)
a2559.name: Minister of Urban Planning
a2559.title: Housing and Sanitation of Benin (report)
a2559.speech: Reported on the preparation of the Urban Development and Decentralisation Support Project (PAURAD) and gave the weekly update on the communal sanitation programme financed by the BOAD and the BIDC, indicating that the works concern the paving and drainage of streets carried out mainly by AGETUR SA, AGETIP BENIN SA and SERHAU SA over a total length exceeding 60,000 linear metres, and urban development and decentralisation support (PAURAD) financed by the IDA involving about ten communes; also reported on the process that led to the selection of a firm to assess the quality of works on the construction site of the new headquarters of the National Assembly.

a2559.speaker: Minister of Public Works and Transport of Benin (report)
a2559.name: Minister of Public Works and Transport of Benin (report)
