a2559.speech: Reported on Benin's participation in the meeting of the steering committee of the project for the development and construction of the Abidjan-Lagos corridor motorway, held in Accra from 17 to 20 September 2013.

a2559.speaker: Minister of Health of Benin (report)
a2559.name: Minister of Health of Benin (report)
a2559.speech: Reported to the Council of Ministers on the visit made last weekend by the President of the Republic to the construction site of the Djidja Zone Hospital.

a2559.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (instructions)
a2559.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (instructions)
a2559.speech: Instructed the Minister of Health to invite the contracting authority AGETIP to take appropriate steps to lift the reservations recorded on the Djidja hospital within a maximum of two weeks and to raise the awareness of the Communal Council with a view to ensuring the cleanliness of the hospital through regular cleaning; and instructed the Minister of Economy and Finance to have prompt arrangements made to release the equipment supplier's material in order to speed up the equipping of the hospital within two months.

a2559.speaker: Secretary General of the Presidency of the Republic of Benin (report)
a2559.name: Secretary General of the Presidency of the Republic of Benin (report)
a2559.speech: Reported to the Council of Ministers on the work plan of the Special Adviser to the Presidency in charge of Governance of Public Enterprises and Internal Control, which will make it possible to ensure that all managers of the eight public enterprises have taken note of the recommendations of the latest management audits and take adequate measures to implement them; to train all members of Boards of Directors on their roles, functioning and governance principles; to have all public enterprises develop or correct their internal control systems; to draft internal procedure manuals; to organise a forum of Directors General of Benin at which the list of the 50 best enterprises will be published; and to have the mission evaluated after six months by an independent team.

a2559.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (decision)
a2559.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (decision)
a2559.speech: In approving this work plan, decided to open a new page in the life of public enterprises in the country through the introduction of a new corporate governance that benefits the productive sector and contributes to the competitiveness of the national economy, and gave instructions to the Special Adviser, in liaison with the Minister of Economy and Finance, to present to the next Council of Ministers an adjusted road map defining a policy and strategy for the sound management of those enterprises, clarifying their missions, defining internal and external control and audit mechanisms, defining management and governing bodies, determining recruitment arrangements for board members and senior managers combining competence with ethics, and drawing up mission letters with obligations as to results; also reiterated its decision to have the accounts of the ORTB and of the SBEE audited.

a2559.speaker: Minister of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries and Minister of Development, Economic Analysis and Forecasting of Benin (report)
a2559.name: Minister of Agriculture
a2559.title: Livestock and Fisheries and Minister of Development, Economic Analysis and Forecasting of Benin (report)
a2559.speech: Reported to the Council of Ministers on the state of agricultural statistics in Benin, noting that the Focal Unit of MCA-Benin, in liaison with the Ministry of Agriculture, requested financing from the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) for an in-depth evaluation of Benin's agricultural statistics system, to be carried out from 12 to 23 May 2014 by an MCC mission in the framework of the formulation of Benin's 2nd compact.

a2559.speaker: Minister at the Presidency of the Republic in charge of coordinating the MDG and SDG implementation policies of Benin (report)
a2559.name: Minister at the Presidency of the Republic in charge of coordinating the MDG and SDG implementation policies of Benin (report)
a2559.speech: Reported to the Council on the progress of the process of implementing the DOING BUSINESS measures.

a2559.speaker: Minister in charge of Relations with Institutions of Benin (report)
a2559.name: Minister in charge of Relations with Institutions of Benin (report)
a2559.speech: Reported to the Council of Ministers on the financial resources requested by the COS LEPI in the framework of the process of updating the national electoral register and the Permanent Computerised Electoral List (LEPI).

a2559.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (instruction)
a2559.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (instruction)
a2559.speech: Instructed the Minister of Economy and Finance to make available to the COS LEPI the sum of two billion CFA francs, bringing total disbursements for the COS-LEPI to 6,111,943,913 CFA francs, and to report on this to the next Council of Ministers.

a2559.speaker: Minister of the Maritime Economy and Port Infrastructure of Benin (report)
a2559.name: Minister of the Maritime Economy and Port Infrastructure of Benin (report)
a2559.speech: Reported to the Council on the tariffs charged at the port of Cotonou to hauliers for the entry and exit of trucks, stating that despite the setting of a single tariff of 10,000 francs, the acting Director General of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou had continued to charge hauliers an additional 5,900 CFA francs in badge fees not paid over to the single window, bringing entry and exit fees to 15,900 francs in disregard of the decisions of the Council of Ministers, and that hauliers reacted on Monday 14 April 2014 by refusing to let trucks into the Port and blocking access number 5.

a2559.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (decision)
a2559.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (decision)
a2559.speech: Taking note of that report, decided to remove Mr Kassim Traore from his functions as acting Director General of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou.

a2559.speaker: Alassani TIGRI, Secretary General of the Government of Benin (signature of the communique)
a2559.name: Alassani TIGRI
a2559.title: Secretary General of the Government of Benin (signature of the communique)
a2559.speech: Done at Porto-Novo, 23 April 2014, The Secretary General of the Government, Alassani TIGRI.

a2687.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia (draft 2025 budget proposal)
a2687.name: Joseph Boakai
a2687.title: President of Liberia (draft 2025 budget proposal)
a2687.speech: In fiscal year 2025, President Joseph Boakai has proposed a budget totaling $851.8 million, of which $745.69 million is allocated for recurrent expenditures, making up 87.5% of the overall budget ; Has proposed an allocation of US$39,886,910 for the National Legislature.

a2687.speaker: Liberian administration
a2687.name: Liberian administration
a2687.speech: Has announced plans to increase civil servants’ salaries by 2025, responding to the pressing issue of low wages in Liberia.

a2687.speaker: Global Competitiveness Index Report (2019)
a2687.name: Global Competitiveness Index Report (2019)
a2687.speech: Highlighted the critical state of infrastructure in Liberia, ranking the country 132nd out of 140 economies assessed for the quality of their infrastructure facilities.

a2687.speaker: World Bank
a2687.name: World Bank
a2687.speech: According to the World Bank, Liberia’s infrastructure stock is significantly below the global standard, which recommends that infrastructure investments should constitute approximately 70 percent of a country’s gross domestic product (GDP) ; The World Bank estimates that Liberia will need to allocate between $350 million and $600 million annually over the next three decades to address these infrastructure deficits.

a2687.speaker: World Bank (on Liberia’s fiscal position)
a2687.name: World Bank (on Liberia’s fiscal position)
a2687.speech: According to the World Bank, Liberia’s fiscal deficit has increased significantly from 1.5 percentage points, now standing at 7.1% of its Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 2023, attributed to a notable decline in revenues and grants, coupled with rising consumption spending by the government ; The World Bank has identified that economic growth begins to suffer significantly when the debt-GDP ratio surpasses a threshold of 77%.

a2687.speaker: Participants at the Third United Nations Conference on Least Developed Countries
a2687.name: Participants at the Third United Nations Conference on Least Developed Countries
a2687.speech: Stressed the critical role of infrastructure development. They stated that building vital infrastructure—such as roads, bridges, and communication systems—is not merely about construction; it is a strategic means to achieve broader developmental outcomes, including the reduction of poverty and the improvement of living conditions for the populace.

a2943.speaker: Annual Report of the African Water Facility January-December 2022 (African Development Bank, June 2023)
a2943.name: Annual Report of the African Water Facility January-December 2022 (African Development Bank
a2943.title: June 2023)
a2943.speech: States that the financial situation of the AWF Special Fund showed 14.29 million euros available to cover new commitments beyond 2022, and that the Facility's performance was judged "solid" as of the end of December 2022; the document indicates that the AWF approached more than 20 potential donors last year with a view to meeting its annual advocacy and resource-mobilisation targets, and that it organised consultations with donors in March 2022 at the 9th World Water Forum in Dakar, Senegal; reports that the Facility had 26 active projects under which 5.12 million euros were disbursed in 2022, that 43 project concepts were reviewed and 20 judged fit for the pipeline, ten projects fully appraised and eight approved for a grant.

a2943.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (pledge)
a2943.name: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (pledge)
a2943.speech: Among the concrete pledges received was that of USAID for US$3 million in unrestricted contributions and technical assistance, in order to support the annual target of mobilising 14 million euros in new commitments.

a2990.speaker: Revised National Decentralisation Policy (Malawi)
a2990.name: Revised National Decentralisation Policy (Malawi)
a2990.speech: The new policy observes that most functions and decision-making processes have been devolved without commensurate financing. It reads: "This is due to the following reasons: (a) The development budget has not been fully devolved; (b) Limited base of own sources of revenue; (c) The specified ceded revenue as a distinct form of revenue for LGAs is not clear; (d) Weak accountability for the limited revenues from the few available; and (e) Poor coordination of development assistance (NGO and Development Partners)." ; "The 1994 Constitution and 1998 Decentralisation Policy designate LGAs as the highest political authority in a district or urban council with deliberative, legislative and executive powers. However, the mandate given to their political functions has often been hindered by insufficient competences of locally elected officials to guide and hold the administration to account and instances of interference in local decision making and implementation from the centre."

a2990.speaker: Hardrod Mkandawire, Malawi Local Government Association executive director
a2990.name: Hardrod Mkandawire
a2990.title: Malawi Local Government Association executive director
a2990.speech: Said high level political will and sincerity among technocrats from the central government was key to meaningful realisation of the aspirations of the new policy.

a2990.speaker: Michael Roscott, World Bank senior public specialist
a2990.name: Michael Roscott
a2990.title: World Bank senior public specialist
a2990.speech: Urged Malawi to ensure that councils are allocated adequate resources for the decentralisation policy to be effective.

a2990.speaker: Shadrack Omol, Unicef country representative
a2990.name: Shadrack Omol
a2990.title: Unicef country representative
a2990.speech: Said if implemented well, decentralisation has many benefits.

a2990.speaker: Richard Chimwendo Banda, Minister of Local Government, Culture and National Unity
a2990.name: Richard Chimwendo Banda
a2990.title: Minister of Local Government, Culture and National Unity
a2990.speech: Called for MDAs to devolve powers to councils for effective implementation of decentralisation.

a2999.speaker: Amb. Iman, Egyptian ambassador
a2999.name: Amb. Iman
a2999.title: Egyptian ambassador
a2999.speech: "The day before yesterday Minister of foreign affairs met with General Taban Deng Gai, the first vice president in New York and during the meeting Egypt pledged assistance in amount of ten million dollar comprising two fish farms as well as solar plant."

a2999.speaker: Taban Deng Gai, First Vice President of South Sudan
a2999.name: Taban Deng Gai
a2999.title: First Vice President of South Sudan
a2999.speech: Has urged the international community to shift their focus from humanitarian assistance to development.

a3074.speaker: SpaceX officials
a3074.name: SpaceX officials
a3074.speech: Confirmed the mission was “go for a spacewalk” after final safety checks of the spacesuits and equipment were carried out.

a3074.speaker: Jared Isaacman, billionaire and founder of Shift4, Polaris Dawn mission commander
a3074.name: Jared Isaacman
a3074.title: billionaire and founder of Shift4, Polaris Dawn mission commander
a3074.speech: “It’s gorgeous,” he said, in awe of what he could see, as he eased out of the spacecraft ; “The handsfree demonstration is very comparable to the trainer, in terms of the foot restraint,” he added, as he tested his spacesuit.

a3074.speaker: Jared Isaacman, billionaire and founder of Shift4, Polaris Dawn mission commander
a3074.name: Jared Isaacman
a3074.title: billionaire and founder of Shift4, Polaris Dawn mission commander
a3074.speech: Had said before lift-off earlier this week: “Whatever risk is associated with it, it is worth it.” ; “I wasn’t alive when humans walked on the moon” ; “I’d certainly like my kids to see humans walking on the moon and Mars, and venturing out and exploring our solar system.”

a3074.speaker: Jared Isaacman, billionaire and founder of Shift4, Polaris Dawn mission commander
a3074.name: Jared Isaacman
a3074.title: billionaire and founder of Shift4, Polaris Dawn mission commander
a3074.speech: Has refused to say how much he is paying for the missions.

a3074.speaker: Sarah Gillis, SpaceX senior engineer and Polaris Dawn crew member
a3074.name: Sarah Gillis
a3074.title: SpaceX senior engineer and Polaris Dawn crew member
a3074.speech: Could be heard saying “pretty good” as she carried out her spacewalk.

a3074.speaker: Sarah Gillis, SpaceX senior engineer and Polaris Dawn crew member
a3074.name: Sarah Gillis
a3074.title: SpaceX senior engineer and Polaris Dawn crew member
a3074.speech: Reported seeing bulges in the hatch seal.

a3074.speaker: SpaceX mission control
a3074.name: SpaceX mission control
a3074.speech: “Pressure indicates good seal,” mission control told the astronauts, reassuringly, as the hatch was shut again.

a3074.speaker: A presenter on the SpaceX live stream
a3074.name: A presenter on the SpaceX live stream
a3074.speech: “That was really cool,” said one of the presenters on the SpaceX live stream.

a3178.speaker: Melanie Roe, Director of Communication Operations for the Millennium Challenge Corporation (Washington)
a3178.name: Melanie Roe
a3178.title: Director of Communication Operations for the Millennium Challenge Corporation (Washington)
a3178.speech: Said she wanted to see how ONIP works, particularly the newspaper "La Nation," and within what framework to continue collaboration on communication for support under the second compact of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA-Benin) ; Wanted to know whether the energy component is essential enough to merit the support of the newspaper "La Nation."

a3178.speaker: Justin Dovoedo, Communication Director of MCA-Benin
a3178.name: Justin Dovoedo
a3178.title: Communication Director of MCA-Benin
a3178.speech: Made a plea for a new form of collaboration, inviting the Director General and her staff to reflect on a new form of partnership that does not necessarily oblige the MCA to spend money.

a3178.speaker: Reine Azifan, Interim Director General of ONIP (National Office of Printing and Press)
a3178.name: Reine Azifan
a3178.title: Interim Director General of ONIP (National Office of Printing and Press)
a3178.speech: Thanked her guests for the honor done to her organization ; Explained that the newspaper "La Nation," although a public service organ, has financial autonomy, so salary and operating costs are the responsibility of the office, which means there is always a counterpart, a sort of win-win partnership between ONIP and the organizations that seek its support; however, bodies such as the MCA that invest in development are not treated in the same way as commercial companies ; Gave the example of UNICEF, which partnered with "La Nation" for media coverage of its activities and in return supports ONIP with computer equipment, cameras and recorders.

a3178.speaker: Bruno Sewade, Editor-in-chief of "La Nation," and Marie-Madeleine Akoffodji, ONIP head of commercial services
a3178.name: Bruno Sewade
a3178.title: Editor-in-chief of "La Nation," and Marie-Madeleine Akoffodji, ONIP head of commercial services
a3178.speech: Gave the assurance that the energy problem is crucial given the load-shedding Benin has been experiencing for years, and pleaded for access to energy for all, but at an acceptable cost.

a3214.speaker: Report of the National Assembly’s joint committee on appropriations
a3214.name: Report of the National Assembly’s joint committee on appropriations
a3214.speech: Revealed that three hundred billion naira of the N700 billion added to the 2025 budget is for procurement of drugs and vaccines ; said this and the requests to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, by some ministries and agencies for more funds, prompted the lawmakers to increase the 2025 budget from N54.2 trillion estimate to N59.77 trillion ; explained that the provision of $200 million (equivalent of N300 billion) for procurement of vaccines and drugs was sequel to the suspension, by the United States Government, of further interventions in Nigeria’s health sector through provision of vaccines and drugs for malaria, Polio, HIV and Tuberculosis using its agency, USAID ; said the suspension of the intervention could have adverse effects on Nigerians affected by such diseases ; “On this note, the president proactively made a new provision of $200 million which is equivalent to N300 billion, in the Service Wide Votes to fill the gap created by the United States (US) Government’s suspension of intervention to Nigerian health sector, to proactively address the abovementioned health challenges which are currently being suffered by countries like Uganda and others.”

a3214.speaker: Report of the National Assembly’s joint committee on appropriations
a3214.name: Report of the National Assembly’s joint committee on appropriations
a3214.speech: Said “after thorough examination” by the committee, additional funds were provided to the agencies, listing the benefitting agencies as including the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU), the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Offences Commission (ICPC), the National Judicial Council (NJC), the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), the Department of State Service (DSS), the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Armed Forces, among others.

a3214.speaker: Bola Ahmed Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a3214.name: Bola Ahmed Tinubu
a3214.title: President of Nigeria
a3214.speech: Had, on December 18, 2024, presented the N49.7 trillion Appropriation Bill to the National Assembly, but requested the lawmakers, on February 5, 2025, to increase the estimates to N54.2 trillion.

a3235.speaker: Henok Tesema, Chief Retail & SME Officer at Awash Bank
a3235.name: Henok Tesema
a3235.title: Chief Retail & SME Officer at Awash Bank
a3235.speech: Expressed the ambition to become one of the top 10 largest banks in the continent as it already hosts 10.4 million customers, during the briefing at the Skylight Hotel on Airport Road.

a3424.speaker: Djanabou Mahonde, UNICEF Representative in Djibouti
a3424.name: Djanabou Mahonde
a3424.title: UNICEF Representative in Djibouti
a3424.speech: In a brief media appearance, said she was honoured to receive, by presidential decree, the medal of Officer in the National Order of 27 June from the hands of the Prime Minister, whom she wished to thank and, through him, the President of the Republic, Mr Ismail Omar Guelleh, and the entire Djiboutian government - for the trust placed in her and in her institution, she specified, and for the excellent collaboration that exists between UNICEF and the various institutions in Djibouti.

a3424.speaker: Djanabou Mahonde, UNICEF Representative in Djibouti
a3424.name: Djanabou Mahonde
a3424.title: UNICEF Representative in Djibouti
a3424.speech: Added that this recognition also bears witness to the mutual trust, the shared respect and the common objectives for the well-being of children, which have produced convincing results.

a3424.speaker: Several guests present at the ceremony (unnamed testimonies)
a3424.name: Several guests present at the ceremony (unnamed testimonies)
a3424.speech: Testimonies gathered from several guests present at the venue corroborated the radiant personality of Mrs Djanabou Mahonde.

a3469.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a3469.name: Donald Trump
a3469.title: US President-elect
a3469.speech: Pledged on Sunday to “stop the transgender lunacy” on day one of his presidency: “I will sign executive orders to end child sexual mutilation, get transgender out of the military and out of our elementary schools and middle schools and high schools,” the president-elect said at an event for young conservatives in Phoenix, Arizona ; he also vowed to “keep men out of women's sports,” adding that “it will be the official policy of the United States government that there are only two genders, male and female.”

a3469.speaker: @foxnews (TikTok post)
a3469.name: @foxnews (TikTok post)
a3469.speech: “'ON DAY ONE': President-elect Trump pledges that he will 'keep men out of women's sports' from the very start of his next term in the White House and sign executive orders that will tackle key issues in the transgender debate.”

a3469.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a3469.name: Donald Trump
a3469.title: US President-elect
a3469.speech: Speaking to the AmericaFest conference, promised immediate measures against “migrant crime,” vowed to designate drug cartels as foreign terrorist organizations, and doubled down on his talk of restoring US control of the Panama Canal ; renewed his vow to immediately begin “the largest deportation operation in American history” upon taking office, and later went further, saying he would “immediately designate the (drug) cartels as foreign terrorist organizations” ; “This criminal network operating on American soil will be dismantled, deported and destroyed,” Trump said.

a3469.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a3469.name: Donald Trump
a3469.title: US President-elect
a3469.speech: Made expansive promises for his second term and drew a dark picture of the four years preceding it: “On January 20, the United States will turn the page forever on four long, horrible years of failure, incompetence, national decline, and we will inaugurate a new era of peace, prosperity and national greatness,” Trump said, referring to his swearing-in ; “I will end the war in Ukraine. I will stop the chaos in the Middle East, and I will prevent, I promise, World War III.” He added: “The golden age of America is upon us.”

a3469.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a3469.name: Donald Trump
a3469.title: US President-elect
a3469.speech: Said Sunday that Panamanian authorities “haven't treated us fairly” in their operation of the Panama Canal; he had said earlier that fees for use of the canal are “ridiculous”; and he added Sunday that if the principles behind the 1970s treaty that gave Panama full control of the canal are not followed, “then we will demand” that it be returned to the United States “in full, quickly and without question.”

a3473.speaker: Abraham Lincoln, cited as one of the American fathers of freedom and democracy
a3473.name: Abraham Lincoln
a3473.title: cited as one of the American fathers of freedom and democracy
a3473.speech: As the American fathers of freedom and democracy, for example Abraham Lincoln, put it, freedom and democracy are “by the people, for the people, of the people.”

a3473.speaker: Abaynehe Girma, author of the article (opinion piece)
a3473.name: Abaynehe Girma
a3473.title: author of the article (opinion piece)
a3473.speech: Argues that freedom and democracy are two sides of one coin and are instruments of peace and for peace; that former colonies have not escaped modern indirect political and economic domination, and that dependence on aid and indebtedness created in the name of development, economic growth and food security erodes a country's and a people's freedom; and that ethnic politics, poverty, cyber-insecurity and climate change all threaten freedom, security and peace.

a3473.speaker: Abaynehe Girma, author of the article (opinion piece)
a3473.name: Abaynehe Girma
a3473.title: author of the article (opinion piece)
a3473.speech: Sets out his observations for Ethiopia: first, that a culture and system of responsibility and accountability must be strengthened; second, that the democratic system must be changed and strengthened through an inclusive-consensus model so that power-sharing and leadership are not determined by the numerical superiority of ethnic groups (“no one left behind by majority rule principle”); third, that democracy must not be measured by the number of political parties (“democracy not for party politics”); fourth, that accountability instruments used under the EPRDF, such as the citizen charter, citizen report card and community scorecard, should be revived and strengthened; fifth, that democracy, justice and freedom must be detached from partisanship and group perspective and citizens treated equally by virtue of citizenship; sixth, that the rule of law must be respected by citizens and law enforcers alike; seventh, that a strong state and a strong, alert civil society are required; and eighth, that the high cost of living, corruption, rent-seeking, kidnapping for ransom, human trafficking and unemployment create crises of livelihood, security and freedom that demand complex, multi-faceted remedies, national resource-mobilisation and investment strategies, corporate social responsibility, and above all political commitment.

a3473.speaker: Ethiopian Reporter (editor's note)
a3473.name: Ethiopian Reporter (editor's note)
a3473.speech: From the editor: the article is partly taken from the author's book “Identity through Conduct and Deed” (2013) and reflects only the author's own viewpoint; he can be reached at his email address.

a3538.speaker: Sidama regional administration (Ethiopia)
a3538.name: Sidama regional administration (Ethiopia)
a3538.speech: Disclosed that it is aggressively working to attract new investments.

a3538.speaker: Desta Ledamo, President of Sidama region
a3538.name: Desta Ledamo
a3538.title: President of Sidama region
a3538.speech: Told Capital that the new region has been focused on ensuring peace and stability, which is now fully achieved: “As an administration that started fully functioning two months ago, besides ensuring the stability of the region we have also focused on the service that we will provide for investors. We have keenly noted the area where we want to accelerate our service provision as per our investors demand, that is, in addition to developing the required infrastructure” ; “We believe that the region has big potential for various investments and to that effect we have commenced promoting the investment opportunities.”

a3538.speaker: Desta Ledamo, President of Sidama region
a3538.name: Desta Ledamo
a3538.title: President of Sidama region
a3538.speech: Said his region has given attention to the expansion of farming, “We are targeted to supply more coffee beans to the central market for export,” and said the region is working on expanding the farmers’ coffee garden and productivity based on the required science ; on value addition, “On the value addition scheme investors have already secured a location at Yirgalem Agro Processing Park, 323 km south of Addis Ababa.”

a3538.speaker: Desta Ledamo, President of Sidama region
a3538.name: Desta Ledamo
a3538.title: President of Sidama region
a3538.speech: “Our region is very close to the central part of the country and also easily accessible by air and in the near future on express road. This is a good opportunity for investment flows in the region besides its resources” ; underlined that peace and security is a priority that the region should ensure more than the experience observed in other regions, and confidently stated that his region is now totally peaceful.

a3601.speaker: James Swan, UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Somalia
a3601.name: James Swan
a3601.title: UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Somalia
a3601.speech: Speaking at a joint press conference following the meeting, emphasized the need for unity and inclusive dialogue among Somalia’s political stakeholders to strengthen state-building and counter the ongoing threat from Al-Shabaab.

a3601.speaker: James Swan, UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Somalia
a3601.name: James Swan
a3601.title: UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Somalia
a3601.speech: stressed the importance of maintaining an open political space to ensure the success of voter registration and direct local council elections. “In that regard, I recalled the importance of an open political environment to permit the successful conduct of elections at all levels,” he said.

a3601.speaker: James Swan, UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Somalia
a3601.name: James Swan
a3601.title: UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Somalia
a3601.speech: acknowledged the deteriorating humanitarian conditions in the region and reaffirmed the UN’s commitment to working with humanitarian partners to provide relief while linking emergency assistance to long-term development goals. “In collaboration with humanitarian partners, the United Nations is working hand-in-hand with the South West State authorities to address these urgent needs,” Mr. Swan said. “And we want to give priority to those who most need assistance. We also, of course, want to link the humanitarian response to this state’s longer-term development needs.”

a3601.speaker: James Swan, UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Somalia
a3601.name: James Swan
a3601.title: UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Somalia
a3601.speech: spoke to South West State’s steadfastness in the fight against the Al-Shabaab terrorist group. “I commend the ongoing efforts by the Somali National Army and South West State forces to defend and recover territory in different regions of the state,” Mr. Swan said. “These efforts are testament to the courage and tenacity of the Somali forces battling Al-Shabaab.”

a3601.speaker: James Swan, UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Somalia
a3601.name: James Swan
a3601.title: UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Somalia
a3601.speech: concluded his remarks by reaffirming the UN’s continued support for South West State’s governance agenda and thanked President Laftagareen for his cooperation and leadership during a pivotal period for Somalia.

a3601.speaker: 28 international partners, including the United Nations (joint statement)
a3601.name: 28 international partners
a3601.title: including the United Nations (joint statement)
a3601.speech: A joint statement from 28 international partners, including the United Nations, earlier last month backed the president’s initiative and stressed the urgency of aligning political efforts to combat Al-Shabaab and implement direct elections.

a3826.speaker: Experts in the sector (construction/3D printing specialists)
a3826.name: Experts in the sector (construction/3D printing specialists)
a3826.speech: Explain that the huge machine can carry out construction quickly according to the design it is given ; explain that the technology makes it possible to execute building domes and structures of high architectural artistry with the required quality ; say that, beyond eliminating the plastering, block-laying and similar processes involved in traditional construction, 3D concrete printing technology reduces the waste of construction inputs ; state that the technology does not require a large workforce and helps to carry out continuous, uninterrupted construction work.

a3826.speaker: Studies conducted in the sector
a3826.name: Studies conducted in the sector
a3826.speech: Show that the technology makes it possible to use construction raw materials that are environmentally friendly and cause low pollution.

a4076.speaker: Ben Cardin, U.S. Senator (D-Md.), Chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee
a4076.name: Ben Cardin
a4076.title: U.S. Senator (D-Md.), Chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee
a4076.speech: "Republicans are squandering two decades of bipartisan success in the fight against AIDS and undermining one of our most effective tools of soft power in a shameful bid to appease extremists interest groups, and I cannot fathom why." ; Marked the day after World AIDS Day by calling attention to the urgent need for Congress to reauthorize the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), which has yet to secure a clean, multi-year renewal. ; "PEPFAR is more than a program - it's a pillar of hope. For decades, it has delivered lifesaving care to millions worldwide, trained healthcare workers, and brought us to the brink of ending HIV/AIDS. But with each day that Congress fails to authorize its five-year renewal, that hope dims, putting the lives of vulnerable children, mothers, and communities at even greater risk." ; "PEPFAR has always stood apart from politics, proving America's strength lies in its common values. Walking away now undermines progress, destabilizes programs like Safe Birth Healthy Babies that prevent mother-to-child HIV transmission, and weakens U.S. global health leadership, leaving partners doubting U.S. leadership and commitment to saving lives." ; "The stakes couldn't be clearer. In the wake of World AIDS Day, this moment calls for decisive action, not delay. Congress must pass a clean, five-year reauthorization of PEPFAR to fulfill America's leadership in the fight against HIV/AIDS and uphold its commitment to a future free from this devastating epidemic."

a4218.speaker: Professor Douglas Boateng, Professor Extraordinaire for Supply Chain Governance and Industrialisation (opinion article)
a4218.name: Professor Douglas Boateng
a4218.title: Professor Extraordinaire for Supply Chain Governance and Industrialisation (opinion article)
a4218.speech: Argues that the United States’ systematic reduction of financial support to foreign nations, including Africa, “is neither a curse nor a crisis. It is, in fact, a clarion call: a moment for Africa to finally stand on its own feet and embrace the principle of Africa First” ; writes that “If America First is a strategy, then Africa First must be a necessity,” and that “a fractured continent cannot rise as one,” with 54 nations operating in silos while together they could wield the power of over 1.3 billion people ; states that the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) “represents the single most transformative economic initiative in Africa’s modern history” but that “Trade agreements do not create prosperity: actions do” ; on aid, writes that foreign aid “has also created an unhealthy dependency,” that with America turning inward Africa faces the end of aid as it once knew it, and that “This is not a tragedy. It is a wake-up call… Foreign aid has rarely been given without strings attached. It has influenced policies, dictated economic directions, and in many cases, kept African nations in cycles of controlled development rather than true independence.” ; concludes “A borrowed clock never tells the right time… AFRICA FIRST. NOT LATER. NOT MAYBE. NOW.”

a4218.speaker: IMF, Statista, World Bank and Bloomberg data (2021-2024), cited as source of GDP figures
a4218.name: IMF
a4218.title: Statista, World Bank and Bloomberg data (2021-2024), cited as source of GDP figures
a4218.speech: Average figures from various data sources, including IMF, Statistica, World Bank, and Bloomberg, amongst others, 2021-2024, cited for the GDP comparisons between US states, European countries and African economies (California $4.0 trillion; Texas $2.4 trillion; New York State $2.2 trillion; Germany $4.5 trillion; Netherlands $1.0 trillion; Nigeria $477 billion; South Africa $399 billion; Egypt $474 billion; Kenya $110 billion; Ghana $82 billion).

a4332.speaker: Givemore Makoni, Zimbabwe Cricket (ZC) Managing Director
a4332.name: Givemore Makoni
a4332.title: Zimbabwe Cricket (ZC) Managing Director
a4332.speech: Welcomed MCC's return, describing it as a momentous occasion for both cricketing and diplomatic ties: "We are proud and thrilled to welcome MCC back to Zimbabwe after six decades." ; "This historic tour is a celebration of our cricketing heritage, an inspiration for our players and fans and a testament to the enduring friendship and cultural ties between Zimbabwe and England."

a4332.speaker: Rob Lynch, MCC's Director of Cricket and Operations
a4332.name: Rob Lynch
a4332.title: MCC's Director of Cricket and Operations
a4332.speech: Said the club was looking forward to the tour: "We are pleased to be touring a Full Member nation as part of our overseas programme this year, with a focus on elite performance."

a4332.speaker: Rob Lynch, MCC's Director of Cricket and Operations
a4332.name: Rob Lynch
a4332.title: MCC's Director of Cricket and Operations
a4332.speech: "This is an exceptionally talented squad, with several players excelling in the domestic game and others with the potential to do so." ; "The relaunch of the MCC Young Cricketers programme this summer was a success, and we're thrilled to include a player who impressed through the scheme."

a4456.speaker: Brigadier General Mohamed Tomba, Minister of State for the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration of Niger (decrees of 12 November)
a4456.name: Brigadier General Mohamed Tomba
a4456.title: Minister of State for the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration of Niger (decrees of 12 November)
a4456.speech: Decided to suspend the activities of two major NGOs, ACTED (Agency for Aid to Cooperation and Development) and APBE (Action for Well-Being), by decrees dated 12 November; the official reasons for the suspension were not clearly stated.

a4456.speaker: Concurring sources (anonymous)
a4456.name: Concurring sources (anonymous)
a4456.speech: Point to concerns linked to national security and to compliance with the regulations in force.

a4456.speaker: Nigerien authorities
a4456.name: Nigerien authorities
a4456.speech: Say the broader policy of surveillance and regulation of NGO activities on national territory aims to strengthen the governance of humanitarian interventions and to ensure the protection of national interests.

a4456.speaker: Government of Niger
a4456.name: Government of Niger
a4456.speech: While affirming its commitment to humanitarian principles, stresses the need for strict regulation to prevent any activity liable to compromise national security.

a4826.speaker: Cho Tae-yul, South Korean Foreign Minister
a4826.name: Cho Tae-yul
a4826.title: South Korean Foreign Minister
a4826.speech: said South Korea was ready to help aid Syria's recovery from its 13-year civil war through business investment and humanitarian assistance.

a4826.speaker: Asaad al-Shaibani, Syrian Foreign Minister
a4826.name: Asaad al-Shaibani
a4826.title: Syrian Foreign Minister
a4826.speech: said he hoped that Seoul would support the easing of international sanctions that remain on Damascus, according to a readout from South Korea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

a4826.speaker: Yonhap news agency (South Korea)
a4826.name: Yonhap news agency (South Korea)
a4826.speech: reported that the establishment of formal ties concludes talks that began in February with approval given by Seoul's cabinet.

a4826.speaker: Yoon Suk-yeol, impeached South Korean President
a4826.name: Yoon Suk-yeol
a4826.title: impeached South Korean President
a4826.speech: set off a political crisis in December when he briefly declared martial law, claiming that "antistate" and North Korean forces had infiltrated the government.

a4850.speaker: Samantha Power, USAID Administrator
a4850.name: Samantha Power
a4850.title: USAID Administrator
a4850.speech: Once asserted that aid is America's soft power, subtly influencing global politics.

a4850.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a4850.name: Abiy Ahmed (PhD)
a4850.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a4850.speech: Expressed the sentiment that "Borrowing from the IMF and the World Bank is like borrowing from your mother."

a4850.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a4850.name: Abiy Ahmed (PhD)
a4850.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a4850.speech: In a declaration four years ago, revealed his economic model as capitalism.

a4850.speaker: Adam Smith, in "The Wealth of Nations"
a4850.name: Adam Smith
a4850.title: in "The Wealth of Nations"
a4850.speech: Underscores the importance of human capital, positing that the "acquired and useful abilities of individuals" are crucial for a nation's wealth and progress.

a4874.speaker: Djibouti Red Crescent (institutional position)
a4874.name: Djibouti Red Crescent (institutional position)
a4874.speech: "Disability must never be an obstacle" - such was the conviction that led the Djibouti Red Crescent to demonstrate once again its commitment to inclusion and human dignity.

a4874.speaker: Amina Houssein Farah, Secretary General of the Djibouti Red Crescent
a4874.name: Amina Houssein Farah
a4874.title: Secretary General of the Djibouti Red Crescent
a4874.speech: In her address, praised the determination of the participants and reaffirmed the will of the Djibouti Red Crescent to continue its inclusive actions.

a4877.speaker: M23 rebels (backed by Rwanda)
a4877.name: M23 rebels (backed by Rwanda)
a4877.speech: Declared on Thursday that they wanted to take their fight to the distant capital, Kinshasa ; also said they would be open to dialogue with the Congolese government, as they sought to assert their control over the city of Goma in the east of the country and the surrounding territory ; asked residents to go about their daily business while the rebels worked to facilitate the delivery of the badly needed humanitarian aid.

a4877.speaker: Corneille Nangaa, one of the political leaders of the M23
a4877.name: Corneille Nangaa
a4877.title: one of the political leaders of the M23
a4877.speech: "We will fight him until we reach Kinshasa," he declared at a press briefing.

a4877.speaker: Corneille Nangaa, one of the political leaders of the M23
a4877.name: Corneille Nangaa
a4877.title: one of the political leaders of the M23
a4877.speech: "We are open to any discussion, but a discussion must take place between the Kinshasa regime and our organisation. We are open to direct discussions," Nangaa said.

a4877.speaker: Corneille Nangaa, one of the political leaders of the M23
a4877.name: Corneille Nangaa
a4877.title: one of the political leaders of the M23
a4877.speech: Rejected the allegations that this was a battle for resources, describing them as "Kinshasa propaganda," insisting that "our struggle is to restore this State, to feed the people" ; said the rebels' objective was "to launch development, to make people live together in peace, but also to create opportunities for the region and for the whole world."

a4877.speaker: UN experts
a4877.name: UN experts
a4877.speech: According to UN experts, the M23 rebels are backed by some 4,000 soldiers from neighbouring Rwanda, far more than in 2012 when they took the city of Goma.

a4877.speaker: Félix Tshisekedi, Congolese President
a4877.name: Félix Tshisekedi
a4877.title: Congolese President
a4877.speech: Called for a massive military mobilisation to resist the rebellion, calling on young people to enlist en masse in the army ; in his first public statements since the M23 rebels' advance into Goma on Monday, promised "a vigorous and coordinated response" to push back the rebels while reaffirming his commitment to a peaceful resolution.

a4877.speaker: Rwandan President
a4877.name: Rwandan President
a4877.speech: Also threatened to "face up to" any confrontation with South Africa.

a4877.speaker: South Africa
a4877.name: South Africa
a4877.speech: Complained that the fighting in eastern Congo has caused deaths among South African peacekeepers.

a4877.speaker: Crucial meeting of neighbouring countries
a4877.name: Crucial meeting of neighbouring countries
a4877.speech: Asked the Congolese government to hold talks with the rebels.

a5049.speaker: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia (data)
a5049.name: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia (data)
a5049.speech: Ministry of Health data for 2024 indicates that 404 hospitals, 3,907 health centres and 15,531 health posts are in service; the ministry, along with international institutions, has testified that Ethiopia registered significant growth in the health sector over the past three decades, raising primary health institution coverage from 50.7 percent in 2000 to 90 percent in 2019.

a5049.speaker: International reports
a5049.name: International reports
a5049.speech: Say the country has 17,534 health posts including those under construction, 3,643 health stations including some 57 under construction, about 3,867 private clinics, and 43 private hospitals.

a5049.speaker: Various reports (on the health sector's problems)
a5049.name: Various reports (on the health sector's problems)
a5049.speech: Classify the problems of Ethiopia's health sector into five main categories: shortage of doctors and professionals (Limited Number of Medical Graduates), professional migration (Brain Drain), Inadequate Infrastructure, Uneven Distribution of infrastructure, and Financial Constraints.

a5049.speaker: Yonatan Dagnew, President of the Ethiopian Health Professionals Association
a5049.name: Yonatan Dagnew
a5049.title: President of the Ethiopian Health Professionals Association
a5049.speech: Says the health sector is distinct: "The work is directly connected with human life. It has a high workload, it demands strict ethics and discipline, and it does not allow one to live while doing other additional jobs as in other professions. Because the health sector is complex in its own right, it requires special attention. It is because that has not happened, and because some of the demands we raised earlier were not properly answered, that the demand is now being raised."

a5049.speaker: Yonatan Dagnew, President of the Ethiopian Health Professionals Association
a5049.name: Yonatan Dagnew
a5049.title: President of the Ethiopian Health Professionals Association
a5049.speech: Explained that medical professionals' demand for salary and benefits should not be seen as a peculiar sin or a luxury, and added that they work facing great danger to serve their country where conditions are not favourable and infrastructure is lacking: "These professionals work by exposing themselves to danger, without excluding patients infected with rapidly transmissible diseases. They have to treat patients with tuberculosis, hepatitis and other diseases while facing danger. Because doctors spend their working day inside a medical institution, they are made more vulnerable than a person who spends the day in an office or a factory. Doctors' protest and demand must be viewed in relation to the overall pressure and nature of the work that the sector demands."

a5049.speaker: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia (data)
a5049.name: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia (data)
a5049.speech: Indicated that about 42,000 health extension workers deployed under 15,000 health posts are providing a major service by delivering community-based health care.

a5049.speaker: Protesting health professionals (placards at demonstrations)
a5049.name: Protesting health professionals (placards at demonstrations)
a5049.speech: Carried placards reading "We are hungry" and "We can no longer survive" at peaceful demonstrations in the regions and at health institutions, saying salary and benefits have become difficult for them.

a5049.speaker: A doctor, member of the Health Professionals Movement association (anonymous)
a5049.name: A doctor
a5049.title: member of the Health Professionals Movement association (anonymous)
a5049.speech: Said that professionals' very existence has today fallen into danger: "It is a problem accumulated and overflowing over the ages that has brought us to this stage. We have been presenting about 12 clearly known demands. Since 2010/11 E.C. we have been presenting our demands clearly, orally and in writing, at the level of the Prime Minister. Of these demands, the main and fundamental one, which could answer 11 of them, is our demand that the medical sector be separated from the civil service and be administered autonomously by a board. Just as it was said that our universities should be organized autonomously, the demand that the health sector too be autonomous and be led by a board managed directly by professionals rather than by politicians has not been answered. It was believed that this would modernize the service and not only satisfy the client but also benefit the professional. The key issue is that an independent board called the Ethiopian National Health Service Board be established. It has also been successful in the experience of Kenya and other countries. If there is a health service not burdened by politics, the suffering and emigration of doctors will stop. Projects come, saying doctors should benefit. Words centred on the professional are promised. It is said you will become a homeowner, there will be money for buying a car, and so on. But nothing ever materializes."

a5049.speaker: Yonatan Dagnew, President of the Ethiopian Health Professionals Association
a5049.name: Yonatan Dagnew
a5049.title: President of the Ethiopian Health Professionals Association
a5049.speech: Stated that the cancellation of USAID and other foreign funding for Ethiopia's health sector is unrelated to the doctors' protest, saying that although the matter may cause damage, the problem is not beyond the country's capacity.

a5049.speaker: A doctor, member of the Health Professionals Movement association (anonymous)
a5049.name: A doctor
a5049.title: member of the Health Professionals Movement association (anonymous)
a5049.speech: Gave an idea supporting the view that the USAID cuts are not the cause, noting that Ethiopia has never poured adequate resources into the health sector.

a5049.speaker: Ministry of Finance of Ethiopia (2017 E.C. budget plan)
a5049.name: Ministry of Finance of Ethiopia (2017 E.C. budget plan)
a5049.speech: Ranks the annual budget allocations by sector, with debt payment leading at 139.31 billion birr (18 percent of the total budget), road development 86 billion birr (11.71 percent), education 79.84 billion birr (10.87 percent), defence 65.70 billion birr (about 8.9 percent), and health fifth at about 33.90 billion birr (about 4.62 percent), followed by justice and security (27.64 billion birr, 3.76 percent), water and energy (25.26 billion birr, 3.44 percent), agriculture (22.92 billion birr, 3.12 percent), disaster prevention (11.90 billion birr, 1.62 percent) and transport and communications (11.89 billion birr, 1.62 percent).

a5049.speaker: UNICEF (report comparing Ethiopia's 2022/23 and 2023/24 budget performance)
a5049.name: UNICEF (report comparing Ethiopia's 2022/23 and 2023/24 budget performance)
a5049.speech: Places the health budget in eighth place, after debt payment, roads, education, defence and other expenditures, and states that Ethiopia allocated 3.4 percent and then 3.9 percent of its total budget to health in the two budget years, a growth of only 0.5 percent.

a5049.speaker: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia (data)
a5049.name: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia (data)
a5049.speech: Indicated that community-based health insurance coverage was extended to 1,050 woredas as of last year (2016 E.C.), with about 11.14 million households benefiting, about 73 percent of the population believed to be reachable.

a5049.speaker: Girma Ababi (Dr.), chairperson of the founding committee of the 'Family Health and Life Insurance' Share Company
a5049.name: Girma Ababi (Dr.)
a5049.title: chairperson of the founding committee of the 'Family Health and Life Insurance' Share Company
a5049.speech: Said the insurance sector accounts for one percent of the country's economy and is still undeveloped: "In Kenya, beyond conventional insurance, they have made the health insurance sector one that moves 66 billion birr in assets. With us, let alone health insurance, the insurance sector as a whole has not yet grown. Health insurance is not given separately on its own by an insurance institution; it is combined with other insurance branches. Although community-based health insurance was started, it has not yet reached everyone. Beyond filling this gap, private health operators need money to grow themselves and for new investment. Therefore, alongside the insurance, we have begun to organize a microfinance bank that provides financial support only to the health sector."

a5049.speaker: Doctors / health professional associations
a5049.name: Doctors / health professional associations
a5049.speech: Announced, through various associations, a one-month deadline for staging a general work stoppage ; said that only one day remains before that deadline expires.

a5049.speaker: Kasahun Follo, President of the Confederation of Ethiopian Trade Unions (CETU)
a5049.name: Kasahun Follo
a5049.title: President of the Confederation of Ethiopian Trade Unions (CETU)
a5049.speech: Said that the doctors' demand has not come to them and that it does not concern them.

a5049.speaker: Civil Servants Proclamation No. 1064/2017 (law)
a5049.name: Civil Servants Proclamation No. 1064/2017 (law)
a5049.speech: Provides in Part Three, Sub-part One, Article Nine for how the salary scale is to be revised, and in Article 17 stipulates that a Merit and Salary Board shall be established for this purpose and shall be chaired by the Prime Minister - indicating that the doctors' salary and benefit demand must pass through long legal and procedural chains.

a5049.speaker: Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2011 (law)
a5049.name: Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2011 (law)
a5049.speech: Provides in Part Nine, Article 137, sub-article two, a list by name of the sectors in which work must not stop whatever the labour dispute: (a) airline services; (b) electric light and power enterprises; (c) water service and urban sanitation enterprises; (d) urban light rail transport services; (e) hospitals, clinics, pharmaceutical distribution enterprises and pharmacies; (f) fire brigade services; and (g) telecommunication services - stipulating that even if doctors have salary and benefit demands, the sector's service should not be interrupted.

a5049.speaker: Yonatan Dagnew, President of the Ethiopian Health Professionals Association
a5049.name: Yonatan Dagnew
a5049.title: President of the Ethiopian Health Professionals Association
a5049.speech: Stated that law is made by people themselves so that people may be governed by it; saying the doctors are presenting a peaceful and civilized demand, he said he believes that even if the law prohibits a work stoppage, before it comes to that the government will look at the matter in good faith and resolve the problems through discussion.

a5049.speaker: A doctor, member of the Health Professionals Movement association (anonymous)
a5049.name: A doctor
a5049.title: member of the Health Professionals Movement association (anonymous)
a5049.speech: Noted that the matter is connected with existence and that people give matters of existence precedence over law, and stated that he expects the government to recognize the urgency of the doctors' peacefully presented demand and move to resolve it.

a5102.speaker: Yene Assegid (PhD), founder of the EveryonesWorld Leadership Foundation program (ELF)
a5102.name: Yene Assegid (PhD)
a5102.title: founder of the EveryonesWorld Leadership Foundation program (ELF)
a5102.speech: “ELF is the only global online Leadership Development Program dedicated to young women aged between 16 and 21. It is designed and delivered by seasoned coaches and leadership practitioners. Each course is three months long and there will be three in a year. The ELF program aims to help young women discover their own expression of leadership and learn to apply it. They will learn competences such as emotional intelligence, conflict management, time management and be given the opportunity to explore their life’s vision, to reflect on their life’s purpose and engage in an intentional life path. All the learning in lectures, coaching and in peer group discussions will be framed by the four pillars of self-responsibility, environmental responsibility, social responsibility and financial responsibility. ELF will provide a space where young women – along with their peers from around the world, will be able to harness their own potential and evolve in accordance with their own vision of their lives. The ELF Program will also support young women to expand their career and professional paths by holding regular talks with various guest speakers who will share about their own life paths, the challenges they faced, and what keeps them motivated.”

a5102.speaker: Yene Assegid (PhD), founder of ELF
a5102.name: Yene Assegid (PhD)
a5102.title: founder of ELF
a5102.speech: On the benefits of joining the training: “The ELF program is a space where young women will be nurtured and developed; they will be introduced to leadership development, professional coaching and will be exposed to other cultures and individuals from around the world.”

a5102.speaker: Yene Assegid (PhD), founder of ELF
a5102.name: Yene Assegid (PhD)
a5102.title: founder of ELF
a5102.speech: On limiting participants to 100: “The first intake in January 2021 is the inaugural cohort; we call those participants Founding Members. They will be pioneers in a brand new program which will certainly grow course by course. Our Founding Members will always be the ones that new participants look to for guidance and inspiration as they embark on the journey.”

a5102.speaker: Yene Assegid (PhD), founder of ELF
a5102.name: Yene Assegid (PhD)
a5102.title: founder of ELF
a5102.speech: On the 16-to-21 age limit: “We want to have young women who are between the age of finishing secondary school and before finishing college. This is a very special age and we feel that if we can equip young women at this age with leadership skills, it will have the most impact. I am sure all of us, at some point, have wished that at that age we were given better guidance about our futures, and more practical wisdom to help us tackle those tricky years of moving from one phase of our lives into the next. It will be a bit like being taken aside by older, successful women who will tell you what they wished they had been told at that age.”

a5102.speaker: Yene Assegid (PhD), founder of ELF
a5102.name: Yene Assegid (PhD)
a5102.title: founder of ELF
a5102.speech: On reaching girls in sub-Saharan Africa without internet or smart devices: “The program is fully online and is available to all young women everywhere. It is a requirement to have Internet access. Part of the reason why we are developing a scholarship system is to assist participants who are unable to pay the tuition fee and may need some help in Internet access. It is our dream to have the funding for at least 50% of the participants and we are encouraging corporates and other donors to become involved by sponsoring groups of participants... Ideally there will be sponsors who will be able to add some extra funds for certain participants to have Internet access. We are reaching out to certain companies in different regions with this in mind.”

a5276.speaker: UN experts (UNODC drug specialists)
a5276.name: UN experts (UNODC drug specialists)
a5276.speech: Warn that criminals are exploiting the unstable global situation and contributing to it ; according to the UN experts, the cocaine boom is leading not only to more drug deaths but also to more violence between rival criminal organisations involved in drug smuggling, which can also be observed in Western and Central Europe ; the UN drug experts are also watching former and active war zones with concern: in Syria the export and import of the synthetic drug captagon persists stubbornly, and in Ukraine the production of and trade in synthetic drugs has increased during the war.

a5276.speaker: UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), World Drug Report
a5276.name: UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)
a5276.title: World Drug Report
a5276.speech: Reported that the number of drug users worldwide has risen to 316 million people, and noted that criminal groups were exploiting and intensifying the unstable situation in many regions ; the annual report said that among all drugs the market for cocaine is growing the fastest, with illegal cocaine production up by more than a third year-on-year in 2023 to a record 3,708 tonnes ; the UN Office reported a dramatically increased murder rate in Ecuador and growing gang violence in the Caribbean ; the UN Office assumes that 64 million people were drug addicted in 2023, an increase of 13 percent within ten years.

a5276.speaker: Ghada Waly, UNODC Executive Director
a5276.name: Ghada Waly
a5276.title: UNODC Executive Director
a5276.speech: Explained on the International Day against Drug Abuse that consumption is growing faster than the global population, and wrote in the report that at present both a growing demand and a growing supply can be observed: "This is fuelling global instability and further stoking that instability - a vicious circle."

a5276.speaker: Current European study (cited by UNODC)
a5276.name: Current European study (cited by UNODC)
a5276.speech: The office quoted from a current European study that, even though European teenagers aged 15 and 16 consumed an above-average amount of cannabis, the frequency of consumption among young people has declined markedly in recent years.

a5372.speaker: A client of Asli Tarcan Clinic, a 34-year-old teacher from London
a5372.name: A client of Asli Tarcan Clinic
a5372.title: a 34-year-old teacher from London
a5372.speech: "I'd heard Turkey was the place to go, but I needed someone who really understood Afro hair. Aslı Tarcan's team didn't just reassure me—they delivered. I actually cried when I saw the first signs of regrowth."

a5500.speaker: Joseph Utsev, Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation
a5500.name: Joseph Utsev
a5500.title: Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation
a5500.speech: Called for a robust public private partnership investment in the water sector to achieve the SDGs and equitable access to water and sanitation services for Nigerians, and urged state Governors, development partners and the private sector to prioritise more investments in the sector ; assured that the Federal Government would continue to support the states through interventions to achieve access to clean and safe water and improve sanitation for all ; pointed out that Lagos, being the most populous and economically vibrant city in the country, is still grappling with significant challenges in providing adequate water and sanitation services for its teeming population, adding that such public private partnership would ensure a robust collaboration between government agencies and private sector to invest more resources in the water sector ; said the PPPs can also attract private investment, improve efficiency and ensure sustainable service delivery while the government can leverage private sector expertise and capital to upgrade existing water infrastructure and expand coverage to under-served areas ; advocated community based organisations that would mobilise resources and implement low-cost, decentralised solutions tailored to local needs especially in areas of operation and maintenance ; while highlighting the importance of international development assistance, said such partnership was also key in financing water and sanitation projects in Nigeria, adding that the multilateral organisations, bilateral donors and development agencies were also important in providing grants, loans and technical assistance to support water infrastructure development.

a5500.speaker: Joseph Utsev, Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation
a5500.name: Joseph Utsev
a5500.title: Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation
a5500.speech: On the issue of the Cholera outbreak in the country, said his ministry had taken proactive steps to prevent further spread of the water-borne disease, including reactivation of the ministry's laboratories across the six geopolitical zones of the country as well as massive sensitisation of citizens on the need to improve on personal hygiene ; called on State Governors, traditional and religious leaders to scale up campaign against open defecation in their states and build more decent toilets for their people to discourage the practice of open defecation to enable the country achieve open defecation free target by 2025.

a5500.speaker: Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Lagos State Governor
a5500.name: Babajide Sanwo-Olu
a5500.title: Lagos State Governor
a5500.speech: Said his administration has in the last five years been committed to addressing the water needs of the State ; said that despite the efforts of the Lagos State Government, there is still a huge gap in achieving access to clean and safe water for his people ; called for more genuine and practical actions and support from the Federal Government and development partners as well as other critical stakeholders in the water and sanitation sector to address the water needs in the country especially in Lagos State.

a5549.speaker: The columnist (John Pires), speaking to his son
a5549.name: The columnist (John Pires)
a5549.title: speaking to his son
a5549.speech: "Do you see those gaps there?" ... "That's a gateway a problem."

a5549.speaker: Scientists
a5549.name: Scientists
a5549.speech: For decades, have spoken clearly—rising temperatures, disappearing forests, melting ice caps.

a5671.speaker: Mr Sun, head of CHIMBUSCO
a5671.name: Mr Sun
a5671.title: head of CHIMBUSCO
a5671.speech: Presented the business plan for his refinery and bunkering project at DDID, in the continuation of an earlier meeting held on 18 April 2019 in Djibouti.

a5671.speaker: Mayor of Changsha
a5671.name: Mayor of Changsha
a5671.speech: During their exchanges, invited Mr Aboubaker Omar Hadi to take part in the second edition of the CAETE (China-Africa Economic and Trade Expo).

a5714.speaker: The White House
a5714.name: The White House
a5714.speech: Announced that the theme of Trump's speech will be the "renewal of the American dream."

a5714.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5714.name: Donald Trump
a5714.title: US President
a5714.speech: Reportedly threatened, at a tense White House meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, to suspend American aid if Kyiv did not seek a rapid settlement of the conflict.

a5714.speaker: Rossiskaya Gazeta
a5714.name: Rossiskaya Gazeta
a5714.speech: Indicates that the president will highlight the results of his administration, notably massive investments to revive American industry and measures to fight inflation.

a5714.speaker: CNN
a5714.name: CNN
a5714.speech: Reported that Trump's aggressive tariff policy has led to an increase in customs duties on Canada, Mexico and China.

a5714.speaker: TASS
a5714.name: TASS
a5714.speech: Stresses that Trump will insist on strengthening border controls and the fight against illegal immigration.

a5714.speaker: Axios
a5714.name: Axios
a5714.speech: Reveals that the Democrats are preparing various forms of protest, ranging from wearing symbolic clothing to more direct actions, such as walking out of the chamber as a sign of disapproval.

a5714.speaker: CNN
a5714.name: CNN
a5714.speech: Points out that some elected officials intend to denounce the mass elimination of posts in the federal administration orchestrated by Trump and his influential adviser, Elon Musk.

a5756.speaker: Civil society WASH actors (petition to the WASH Legislative Caucus)
a5756.name: Civil society WASH actors (petition to the WASH Legislative Caucus)
a5756.speech: Petitioned the government, through the National Legislature, to prioritise the sector to improve citizens’ livelihoods and the economy, reminding the government that the right to safe water and sanitation services is at the heart of all fundamental human rights ; called on the government to seek additional partnership for grants and loans to complete ongoing projects, that County Development Agenda and resolution include WASH budget, and that the National Legislature take immediate actions to review the budget, engage the Finance Minister and the President to ensure increased financing for WASH, and that the recast national budget for 2025 prioritise the implementation of incomplete WASH projects

a5756.speaker: Windell King, member of the civil society WASH group
a5756.name: Windell King
a5756.title: member of the civil society WASH group
a5756.speech: Highlighted several challenges in the country’s WASH sector, stressing the need for action from stakeholders: “Access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene underpins wider efforts to end poverty, advance other interrelated Sustainable Development Goals and, more importantly, strengthen peace and stability” ; quoting several reports from international organizations, disclosed that as of 2022, 1.3 million people in Liberia, or 1 in 4 of the population, lack access to clean water close to home, that 4.1 million people, 8 in 10 of the population, do not have access to a decent toilet, and that around 1 million people, at least 9 in 10 of the population, lack soap and/or water to wash their hands at home ; “Poor sanitation costs Liberia 17.5 million USD, and over 3000 persons die each year, WSP-2012. Over 50 per cent of HCFs in Liberia lack access to WASH services, JMP 2023” ; reminded government of its commitment in its development agenda to establish an integrated WASH Management Information System, increase safely managed water access to 65 per cent and basic access to 90 per cent, end open defecation and increase safely managed access to sanitation to 50 per cent and basic access to 85 per cent by 2029

a5756.speaker: Thomas Goshua, Chairman of the WASH Legislative Caucus and Grand Bassa County Representative
a5756.name: Thomas Goshua
a5756.title: Chairman of the WASH Legislative Caucus and Grand Bassa County Representative
a5756.speech: Acknowledged challenges in the sector that need the government’s attention and stressed the need for more support to the WASH sector, especially in the midst of declining donor support, particularly from USAID: “The WASH Legislative Caucus’ attention has been drawn to the current withdrawal of major donors’ support and those supporting the WASH sector, and it should be a wakeup call to the Government of Liberia and all citizens to double-up effort to prioritize WASH financing and ensure ownership and sustainability of WASH initiatives in the country” ; assured the petitioners, the entire citizenry, and development partners that the caucus members will begin engaging fellow lawmakers and officials of the Executive to ensure funding is allocated in the 2025 recast budget

a5756.speaker: Timothy Kpeh, Sanitation and Water for All (SWA) CSO Focus Point for Liberia
a5756.name: Timothy Kpeh
a5756.title: Sanitation and Water for All (SWA) CSO Focus Point for Liberia
a5756.speech: Called on President Joseph Boakai to sign the Liberia WASH Compact 2.0 as a means of demonstrating high-level political leadership for WASH, describing the WASH Compact as a Heads of State Initiative intended to help presidents and prime ministers make water, sanitation, and hygiene a national priority ; “These initiatives underpin critical development goals like making communities more resilient to climate change and solving public health crises.”

a5762.speaker: Experts (authors of the study on PEPFAR)
a5762.name: Experts (authors of the study on PEPFAR)
a5762.speech: Assessed the potential impacts on HIV/AIDS treatment and prevention efforts in sub-Saharan Africa if PEPFAR is suspended or receives only limited short-term funding, estimating that more than one million children could be infected with the virus and nearly 500,000 children could die by 2030

a5762.speaker: Lucie Cluver, co-author of the study, University of Oxford
a5762.name: Lucie Cluver
a5762.title: co-author of the study, University of Oxford
a5762.speech: “The future of the programmes is at stake. Losing stable, long-term support sends global progress towards ending HIV/AIDS back to the dark ages of the epidemic, especially where children and adolescents are concerned.”

a5762.speaker: Authors of the study
a5762.name: Authors of the study
a5762.speech: Consider that “a sudden withdrawal of the programmes (...) could lead to a resurgence of HIV infections and preventable deaths, as well as a dramatic increase in the number of children orphaned by AIDS in the coming years” – an estimated 2.8 million – and “a setback that could erode two decades of progress”

a5762.speaker: Chris Desmond, professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, and co-author of the study
a5762.name: Chris Desmond
a5762.title: professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, and co-author of the study
a5762.speech: Stressed “that a well-planned transition to expanded national ownership of PEPFAR programmes is urgently needed, one that will carry this life-saving work forward and offer stability and sustainability for the countries that currently depend on PEPFAR support now and in the future, which in turn also benefits the US and solidifies its position as a global leader in the effort to end HIV”

a5762.speaker: US development agency (USAID)
a5762.name: US development agency (USAID)
a5762.speech: Announced in February of this year that it would cut 92% of funding for programmes abroad

a5856.speaker: Othman Masoud Othman, Zanzibar's First Vice President, national chairperson of ACT Wazalendo and the party's presidential candidate
a5856.name: Othman Masoud Othman
a5856.title: Zanzibar's First Vice President, national chairperson of ACT Wazalendo and the party's presidential candidate
a5856.speech: Meeting Commonwealth Assistant Secretary-General Professor Luis Franceschi at Marlborough House, outlined his vision for Zanzibar's future built on five key pillars: unwavering democratic values; good governance and uncompromising accountability; economic progress under the 'Singapore of Africa' vision; enhanced autonomy for Zanzibar within a just, equitable and respectful Union; and national unity with enduring peace.

a5856.speaker: Othman Masoud Othman, Zanzibar's First Vice President, national chairperson of ACT Wazalendo and the party's presidential candidate
a5856.name: Othman Masoud Othman
a5856.title: Zanzibar's First Vice President, national chairperson of ACT Wazalendo and the party's presidential candidate
a5856.speech: Raised concerns, in a statement released on Wednesday, over a flawed voter registration process and an unconstitutional two-day voting arrangement: "In some situations, you can be fined for reporting cases of election fraud, and voters are turned away from registering to vote. It is the right of all citizens to have access to the voter registration list. We need to remove ghost voters from the voter registry and improve transparency in the Electoral Commission."

a5856.speaker: Othman Masoud Othman, Zanzibar's First Vice President, national chairperson of ACT Wazalendo and the party's presidential candidate
a5856.name: Othman Masoud Othman
a5856.title: Zanzibar's First Vice President, national chairperson of ACT Wazalendo and the party's presidential candidate
a5856.speech: In discussions at Chatham House on inclusive economic development: "If you look at Zanzibar and Mauritius, we have similar population sizes and geographic areas, yet Mauritius' GDP per capita is ten times larger than ours. This is something we urgently need to address. We must ensure that investment in Zanzibar leads to shared prosperity - where we all feel the benefits."

a5856.speaker: Othman Masoud Othman, Zanzibar's First Vice President, national chairperson of ACT Wazalendo and the party's presidential candidate
a5856.name: Othman Masoud Othman
a5856.title: Zanzibar's First Vice President, national chairperson of ACT Wazalendo and the party's presidential candidate
a5856.speech: In his meeting with the UK FCDO on June 17: "Zanzibar is fundamentally a service-based economy, and as a result, corruption is especially ruinous. Elections are not just a political event; their outcomes go to the heart of Zanzibar's development and the lives of its people."

a5856.speaker: Professor Luis Franceschi, Assistant Secretary-General of the Commonwealth
a5856.name: Professor Luis Franceschi
a5856.title: Assistant Secretary-General of the Commonwealth
a5856.speech: Noted that while engagement with Zanzibar's electoral process is already under way, the Commonwealth Secretariat is awaiting an invitation from the mainland to further support democratic efforts across the region; said he was committed to an ongoing dialogue with both Mr Othman and the government of Tanzania as Zanzibar's election draws nearer.

a5856.speaker: Chatham House
a5856.name: Chatham House
a5856.speech: Reaffirmed its intention to increase its focus on Zanzibar specifically, within its broader engagement on Tanzania and the Union.

a5856.speaker: Mehdi Hussain, acting Head of the East Africa Department at the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO)
a5856.name: Mehdi Hussain
a5856.title: acting Head of the East Africa Department at the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO)
a5856.speech: Echoed the UK's strong interest in transparent democratic processes, noting significant investments in Zanzibar's roads and infrastructure and close ties with the islands, with over 42,000 British citizens visiting each year; emphasised that ensuring a free, transparent and secure electoral process directly contributes to Zanzibar's continued development and prosperity.

a5928.speaker: Rev. Baxton Maulidi, All Africa Conference of Churches (AACC) economic justice & accountability champion in Malawi
a5928.name: Rev. Baxton Maulidi
