a5928.title: All Africa Conference of Churches (AACC) economic justice & accountability champion in Malawi
a5928.speech: Advised that, ahead of the 2025 General Elections, the State authorities be extra transparent in the electoral process to avoid any suspicions of rigging; faults the State authorities for lack of continuous update of the Kanengo operations ; “It was not wrong for the Leader of Opposition to visit the place as probably a whistleblower alerted him and the other opposition MPs about some suspicious activities there. Whistleblowers are needed in order to make things right” ; “It is clear, based on the reaction of the rest of the members of the public after the MPs visit to the warehouse, that the majority of people are not aware of this arrangement with NRB at Kanengo. Ahead of the General Elections, all stakeholders are bound to be sensitive to the whole electoral process. All eyes are on the voter registration process and that calls for continuous update for transparency and accountability.”

a5928.speaker: Rev. Baxton Maulidi, All Africa Conference of Churches (AACC) economic justice & accountability champion in Malawi
a5928.name: Rev. Baxton Maulidi
a5928.title: All Africa Conference of Churches (AACC) economic justice & accountability champion in Malawi
a5928.speech: Said the transparency and accountability should also go along with security of every electoral process, saying the warehouse at Kanengo should have been well secured by the country’s law enforcement agency, the Malawi Police Service ; “Part of transparency and accountability in the electoral process is security. It is apparent that the opposition MPs did not find any, thus they can make as many accusations they might make, which unfortunately can be misleading due to lack of security transparency. There have been many other instances where the NRB has been accused of not providing the right services in as far as voter registration is concerned — with many of the issues being controversial and conflicting on the suspicion of rigging of the elections. The State authorities, therefore, must be transparent at every stage of the electoral process by updating the nation of every development because every activity is going to raise eyebrows. For the case of the Kanengo controversy, the State authorities should have come out in the open, along with their development partners, to explain the arrangement and dispel any suspicions of vote rigging instead of letting loose a one-sided version of the event. The nation needs to know all these things. I mean, very few knew of the arrangement between the government, the UNDP and other development partners at Kanengo — thus there was need to keep updating the public of the progress that this system has achieved so far.” ; concluded by saying that while whistleblowing on wrong electoral process is very important, it should also be done in good faith having established all elements of evidence to avoid creating a state of panic among all stakeholders.

a5928.speaker: George Chaponda, Leader of Opposition in Malawi
a5928.name: George Chaponda
a5928.title: Leader of Opposition in Malawi
a5928.speech: Accused the government of using the National Food Reserve Agency (NFRA) warehouse in Kanengo, Lilongwe in collaboration with the National Registration Bureau (NRB), to compromise the ongoing voter registration exercise ; told the august House that the opposition MPs’ visit was initially intended to assess the availability of maize at the warehouses but claims they stumbled upon thousands of national IDs scattered on the warehouse floor, with some packed in sacks; asserted that the NRB’s operation at the NFRA warehouse raised serious questions about the integrity and security of its operations and questioned why the institution, that is critical to electoral processes, was operating from a warehouse rather than its official premises at the Office of the President and Vice-President.

a5928.speaker: National Registration Bureau (NRB) officials
a5928.name: National Registration Bureau (NRB) officials
a5928.speech: Hit back by accusing the MPs of deliberately scattering the items they found before capturing the place on camera strewn with IDs and papers.

a5928.speaker: Junior staff / interns at the Kanengo warehouse (interviewed in the MPs’ video clips)
a5928.name: Junior staff / interns at the Kanengo warehouse (interviewed in the MPs’ video clips)
a5928.speech: Explained that their job as interns was to sort out the cards according to each registration centre and pack them for distribution, and that their seniors were somewhere else on other duties to do with their processes.

a5947.speaker: Fred Boltz, head of programming at the Global Environment Facility (GEF)
a5947.name: Fred Boltz
a5947.title: head of programming at the Global Environment Facility (GEF)
a5947.speech: Told Reuters on the sidelines of a meeting of African environment ministers that the GEF aims to do a wildlife conservation bond for every one of the 54 countries in Africa; said such a move would require an investment of $150 million from GEF, which would then be leveraged 10 times to provide a total of $1.5 billion for conservation efforts through other borrowing; said GEF now hopes they can be expanded to include entire ecosystems such as wetlands.

a5947.speaker: Fred Boltz, head of programming at the Global Environment Facility (GEF)
a5947.name: Fred Boltz
a5947.title: head of programming at the Global Environment Facility (GEF)
a5947.speech: On aid and development funding cuts by the United States and other major economies: “Many countries are asking, are suggesting, that in this tough official development assistance environment, that maintaining the last level of (species) replenishment may be difficult, and that we might need to try to do more with less.”

a5947.speaker: Climate finance experts
a5947.name: Climate finance experts
a5947.speech: Say money borrowed using wildlife bonds does not typically go onto the books of beneficiary governments, meaning they can offer much-needed financing to poorer countries.

a5947.speaker: UN Environment Programme in Africa (@UNEP_Africa) (social media post)
a5947.name: UN Environment Programme in Africa (@UNEP_Africa) (social media post)
a5947.speech: “The ministerial segment of #AMCEN20 has officially opened in Nairobi. As AMCEN marks 40 years, African leaders, ministers, and partners gather to drive forward regional priorities on climate, nature, waste, finance, and resilience. Africa is not waiting, it's leading.”

a5947.speaker: Global Environment Facility (@theGEF) (social media post)
a5947.name: Global Environment Facility (@theGEF) (social media post)
a5947.speech: “Speaking at #AMCEN20, Fred Boltz, Head of Programming @theGEF emphasized the fund's longstanding partnership w/ African leadership in advancing environmental progress & biodiversity efforts. GEF remains committed to ongoing reforms for #GEF9 to enhance efficiency and impact.”

a6088.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6088.name: Augustine K. Ngafuan
a6088.title: Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6088.speech: has emphasized that increasing domestic resource mobilization is essential for the country's growth and development across all sectors ; According to Ngafuan, enhancing domestic resource mobilization will help strengthen governance, fiscal systems, and capital market institutions, reducing the nation's dependency on foreign aid. He added that it would ensure more reliable fiscal revenues, thus reinforcing the social contract between the government and the citizens. ; "The leadership of President Boakai is committed to increasing domestic resources across all sectors, aligning them with the National Development Agenda for inclusive growth and development." ; "This will empower citizens to monitor and supervise budgetary revenues and ensure that they are used for the benefit of the people."

a6088.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6088.name: Augustine K. Ngafuan
a6088.title: Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6088.speech: expressed his gratitude to the Chinese government for their ongoing support to Liberia's health and education sectors. "Your support over the years has been a source of hope for Liberians across the health and education sectors."

a6088.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6088.name: Augustine K. Ngafuan
a6088.title: Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6088.speech: pointed out two major constraints hindering Liberia's growth-energy and road infrastructure. He noted that these are the critical areas the government is currently addressing with the help of its development partners. "Energy and roads are the two huge binding constraints that need a robust solution for our country." ; "We are going to make reforms to the electricity sector across the country and strengthen accountable institutions like the General Auditing Commission, which has been rolling out many audit processes." ; outlined that one of the major projects underway is the construction of a hydro-energy facility on the St. Paul River, estimated to cost around US$800 million.

a6088.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6088.name: Augustine K. Ngafuan
a6088.title: Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6088.speech: According to Ngafuan, the country has already met 14 out of 20 criteria required to qualify for Compact Two. "Our job is to continue showing progress to our people because they deserve better lives, and we are making significant strides toward that."

a6088.speaker: Chinese delegation
a6088.name: Chinese delegation
a6088.speech: praised Ngafuan's leadership, expressed their commitment to supporting Liberia's development efforts.

a6088.speaker: YIN Chengwu, Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Liberia
a6088.name: YIN Chengwu
a6088.title: Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Liberia
a6088.speech: reiterated China's strong partnership with Liberia and affirmed their continued support for the country's national development. "We are willing to support any of your national development and infrastructure projects across Liberia."

a6088.speaker: YIN Chengwu, Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Liberia
a6088.name: YIN Chengwu
a6088.title: Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Liberia
a6088.speech: noted the two countries' shared experiences in combating Ebola and COVID-19 and their fruitful cooperation in various areas of national development. "Liberia and China enjoy a long-standing, friendly relationship. In recent years, the Chinese and Liberian people have stood together in the joint fight against Ebola and COVID-19 and have engaged in sincere cooperation in the cause of national development."

a6192.speaker: UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) reports
a6192.name: UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) reports
a6192.speech: State that more than 400,000 people have fled their homes since the beginning of 2025 because of the fighting.

a6192.speaker: Human rights organisations
a6192.name: Human rights organisations
a6192.speech: Have accused the M23 group of human rights violations, including the killing and rape of civilians.

a6192.speaker: Aid organisations
a6192.name: Aid organisations
a6192.speech: Said that hospitals have been overwhelmed with hundreds of people wounded in the fighting, including children.

a6192.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6192.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6192.speech: Has said that the distribution of food aid has been temporarily suspended in and around Goma because of the fighting.

a6192.speaker: Jens Laerke, spokesperson of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
a6192.name: Jens Laerke
a6192.title: spokesperson of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
a6192.speech: Has said there were many bodies of people who had been killed lying in the streets.

a6192.speaker: Red Cross
a6192.name: Red Cross
a6192.speech: Has warned that the continuation of the fighting in Goma risks the spread of dangerous diseases, including Ebola, if the laboratories holding samples of that virus are destroyed in the violence.

a6192.speaker: Government of South Africa
a6192.name: Government of South Africa
a6192.speech: Has confirmed that peacekeeping soldiers from South Africa were killed in the fighting.

a6192.speaker: Government of DRC President Felix Tshisekedi
a6192.name: Government of DRC President Felix Tshisekedi
a6192.speech: Wrote a letter to the African Union Peace and Security Council (PSC) requesting that an emergency meeting be convened over the continuing fighting.

a6192.speaker: Government of the DRC (letter of 17 December 2024 to the UN Security Council)
a6192.name: Government of the DRC (letter of 17 December 2024 to the UN Security Council)
a6192.speech: Blamed Rwanda for delaying talks by insisting on direct negotiations with M23.

a6192.speaker: Rwanda
a6192.name: Rwanda
a6192.speech: Denied those accusations in its response of 19 December 2024; has consistently denied allegations that it supports the M23 rebel group, saying the conflict involves internal DRC matters.

a6192.speaker: United States, Britain and France
a6192.name: United States
a6192.title: Britain and France
a6192.speech: Have condemned Rwanda's act of supporting the M23 rebel group.

a6192.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a6192.name: Marco Rubio
a6192.title: US Secretary of State
a6192.speech: Has asked the United Nations Security Council to consider steps to halt the attacks being carried out by Rwandan troops and M23 rebels in eastern DRC ; said that the United States wants the fighting to stop and called on all sides to respect the borders of a sovereign nation.

a6192.speaker: United States Embassy in Kinshasa
a6192.name: United States Embassy in Kinshasa
a6192.speech: Has urged its citizens to leave the city of Goma because of the increase in violence.

a6192.speaker: United Nations Group of Experts (December report)
a6192.name: United Nations Group of Experts (December report)
a6192.speech: Said that at least 150 tonnes of coltan were smuggled to Rwanda and mixed with Rwandan minerals ; added: "Since April 2024, M23 with the support of the RDF (Rwanda Defence Force) has made gains in controlling new areas."

a6285.speaker: All Progressives Congress (APC), Delta State chapter
a6285.name: All Progressives Congress (APC)
a6285.title: Delta State chapter
a6285.speech: Has praised the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) for arresting former Delta State Governor Ifeanyi Okowa, describing the move as a “bold step” in Nigeria's ongoing anti-corruption campaign.

a6285.speaker: People's Democratic Party (PDP)
a6285.name: People's Democratic Party (PDP)
a6285.speech: Condemned the arrest, calling it a “political witch hunt” by the APC-led federal government aimed at silencing opposition voices.

a6285.speaker: Valentine Onojeghuo, APC State Publicity Secretary (statement)
a6285.name: Valentine Onojeghuo
a6285.title: APC State Publicity Secretary (statement)
a6285.speech: In a statement, the party urged the EFCC to widen its investigation to include other officials suspected of financial mismanagement. “Dr. Ifeanyi Okowa's administration has long been plagued by allegations of financial misconduct and diversion of public funds, which must now be fully addressed,” Onojeghuo said ; added that the arrest should act as a deterrent to other public officials, asserting, “The era of impunity is over. No one is above the law, regardless of their position or connections.” He further stressed the importance of ensuring that public resources serve the people rather than personal interests, saying, “This is a vital step towards restoring public trust.”

a6285.speaker: Timothy Osadolor, PDP Deputy National Youth Leader
a6285.name: Timothy Osadolor
a6285.title: PDP Deputy National Youth Leader
a6285.speech: Argued that Delta State has not reported any missing funds and insisted that detaining Okowa without formal charges undermines democratic principles.

a6285.speaker: Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
a6285.name: Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
a6285.speech: According to the EFCC, the alleged misappropriation involves approximately N1.3 trillion.

a6573.speaker: Allan Tamba, DEC Public Relations Officer (press statement)
a6573.name: Allan Tamba
a6573.title: DEC Public Relations Officer (press statement)
a6573.speech: Said "This arrest is a major milestone in our ongoing efforts to dismantle criminal drug syndicates operating both locally and internationally" ; "Mr Kasolo has been on our radar for some time, and his apprehension sends a strong message that no one is beyond the reach of justice."

a6573.speaker: Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC)
a6573.name: Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC)
a6573.speech: Confirmed that Mr Kasolo is linked to a 2024 case involving the attempted smuggling of 204.7 kilogrammes of cannabis disguised as catalytic powder through Kenneth Kaunda International Airport, destined for Europe.

a6573.speaker: Allan Tamba, DEC Public Relations Officer
a6573.name: Allan Tamba
a6573.title: DEC Public Relations Officer
a6573.speech: Added that "Mr Kasolo was also recently deported from the United States where he was convicted on similar charges" ; "This highlights the global footprint of his criminal activities."

a6642.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) (post on the social network X)
a6642.name: World Food Programme (WFP) (post on the social network X)
a6642.speech: Confirmed that "the recent pause relating to in-kind food assistance to the WFP (purchased from North American farmers with Title II funds) has been revoked", meaning "the resumption of food purchases and deliveries under existing USAID (United States Agency for International Development) agreements", which will allow the UN agency to continue working with partner NGOs, "which play a vital role in distributing emergency food assistance to people affected by wars, floods, droughts and other disasters around the world" ; "The WFP continues to work closely with its North American counterparts and with all our donors to ensure constant and uninterrupted emergency food assistance in hunger hotspots, including Sudan, South Sudan, Gaza, Haiti and other crisis areas."

a6646.speaker: Representative of Senegal before the Fourth Committee of the UN General Assembly
a6646.name: Representative of Senegal before the Fourth Committee of the UN General Assembly
a6646.speech: "Senegal would like to reaffirm unambiguously its recognition of the full sovereignty of the Kingdom of Morocco over the Sahara" ; noted that this position is materialised on the ground by a strong presence of Senegalese nationals in the Kingdom's southern provinces and by the establishment since April 2021 of a consulate general in Dakhla ; reiterated his country's "constant" support for the Moroccan autonomy initiative ; noted that the autonomy plan is consolidated by Morocco's substantial achievements in human rights, notably the role played by the commissions of the National Human Rights Council in Dakhla and Laayoune, and by the investments and projects implemented by the Kingdom under the new development model for the southern provinces, contributing to the empowerment of the populations and the improvement of the human development index in the region ; reaffirmed "total support" for any "initiative going in the direction of the well-being of the populations of the Moroccan Sahara and of the integrity and continuity of the territory of the Kingdom of Morocco."

a6646.speaker: Representative of Senegal before the Fourth Committee of the UN General Assembly
a6646.name: Representative of Senegal before the Fourth Committee of the UN General Assembly
a6646.speech: Welcomed Morocco's full respect of the ceasefire as well as its constant cooperation with MINURSO, calling on the parties for better collaboration with UN entities, notably UNHCR and the WFP, for optimal protection of the rights of the populations of the Tindouf camps, in particular their freedom of expression and association and access to the international humanitarian aid intended for them.

a6646.speaker: Representative of Senegal before the Fourth Committee of the UN General Assembly
a6646.name: Representative of Senegal before the Fourth Committee of the UN General Assembly
a6646.speech: Welcomed the efforts of the UN Secretary-General's Personal Envoy for the Moroccan Sahara, Staffan de Mistura, aimed at facilitating the relaunch of the political process under the exclusive auspices of the United Nations ; called on the main actors in this regional dispute for greater engagement to reach a realistic and lasting political solution, in accordance with international law and the relevant resolutions adopted by the UN Security Council and General Assembly.

a6646.speaker: UN Security Council (successive resolutions since 2007, including resolution 2703)
a6646.name: UN Security Council (successive resolutions since 2007
a6646.title: including resolution 2703)
a6646.speech: Qualifies the Moroccan autonomy initiative as serious and credible in its successive resolutions since 2007, and hailed in resolution 2703 the role played by the commissions of the National Human Rights Council in Dakhla and Laayoune.

a6789.speaker: Adamu Garba, former Nigerian senator and presidential candidate
a6789.name: Adamu Garba
a6789.title: former Nigerian senator and presidential candidate
a6789.speech: Declared on X, in a video, that the elimination of the US development aid agency (USAID), floated by Elon Musk, would be good news for the security of the African continent and for the fight against terrorism; said the US aid agency supports destabilisation operations on the continent and added that without its support terrorist groups such as Boko Haram or Islamic State in West Africa could find themselves short of weapons, ammunition and reconnaissance means: "This is one of the very good pieces of news for Africa, because USAID is an unconventional weapon of war for American special forces, which use methods of psychological manipulation and support insurgency and irregular warfare against Africans." Indicated that USAID's educational or health programmes are only a mask concealing a desire to "disorganise" African countries in order to continue exploiting them and to serve an American agenda.

a6789.speaker: Elon Musk
a6789.name: Elon Musk
a6789.speech: Raised the possibility of eliminating the US development aid agency (USAID).

a6802.speaker: UN High Commissioner for Refugees (message for World Refugee Day 2023)
a6802.name: UN High Commissioner for Refugees (message for World Refugee Day 2023)
a6802.speech: Recounted meeting Abdulaziz Lugazo in the Kakuma refugee camp, who chairs a cooperative of farmers producing drought-resistant crops and who, thanks to Kenya's increasingly inclusive policies, can work land provided by the government and earn enough to pay for his children's school books and uniforms; said Kenya and Kenyans have been generously hosting refugees for more than 30 years and that in his countless visits he has seen the impact of the many positive and concrete measures taken to improve the living conditions of refugees and host communities.

a6802.speaker: UN High Commissioner for Refugees (message for World Refugee Day 2023)
a6802.name: UN High Commissioner for Refugees (message for World Refugee Day 2023)
a6802.speech: Stressed to the rest of the world that “we can — and must — do more to offer hope, opportunities and solutions to refugees, wherever they are and whatever the context. Kenya shows that it is possible”; said integrating refugees into the communities where they have found safety is the most effective way to help them restart their lives and contribute to the growth of host countries, which concretely means ensuring refugees can apply for jobs, enrol in schools and access services such as housing and health care; said at UNHCR “we know that inclusion is the best way to support refugees in exile”.

a6802.speaker: UN High Commissioner for Refugees (message for World Refugee Day 2023)
a6802.name: UN High Commissioner for Refugees (message for World Refugee Day 2023)
a6802.speech: Said host countries cannot achieve this alone and that the rest of the international community must step in and provide the financial resources needed to implement these progressive policies, noting enormous progress in recent years thanks to exceptional donor generosity, innovative approaches to financing and considerable investments from the World Bank, the regional development banks and other international financial institutions, “but it is clear that more must be done”; said many host countries, like Sudan's neighbours, have the will to welcome and integrate refugees but need far more investment and support.

a6802.speaker: UN High Commissioner for Refugees (message for World Refugee Day 2023)
a6802.name: UN High Commissioner for Refugees (message for World Refugee Day 2023)
a6802.speech: Called on leaders to live up to their responsibility to negotiate peace so that the violence stops and refugees can return home safely and voluntarily; asked governments to increase resettlement opportunities for refugees who desperately need them; and called on States to adopt policies that harness the enormous potential of refugees to contribute to the social, economic and political life of host countries, warning “we know all too well the cost of inaction: a world with the highest levels of forced displacement in history. We cannot let this situation continue.”

a7029.speaker: Dr Yanmar Ortese, Benue State Commissioner for Health and Human Services
a7029.name: Dr Yanmar Ortese
a7029.title: Benue State Commissioner for Health and Human Services
a7029.speech: Made the disclosure that a total of 180,000 people living with HIV are now accessing life-saving antiretroviral treatment across 264 health facilities in Benue State, while commending the APIN public health initiative and the United States Centre for Disease Control (US CDC) for donating a cutting-edge Molecular Laboratory and a Polymerase Chain Reaction machine to the Federal Medical Centre (FMC) in Makurdi; was full of praises for the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) for its support to the state in the fight against HIV/AIDS ; “Your investment in our healthcare system has been instrumental in transforming HIV from a death sentence to a manageable chronic disease” ; “Through PEPFAR's support, over 180,000 people living with HIV are now accessing life-saving antiretroviral treatment across 264 health facilities in our state” ; “The prevention of mother-to-child transmission programme has also ensured the birth of approximately 8,000 HIV-negative babies annually.”

a7029.speaker: Professor Joseph Kortor, Medical Director of the Federal Medical Centre (FMC) Makurdi
a7029.name: Professor Joseph Kortor
a7029.title: Medical Director of the Federal Medical Centre (FMC) Makurdi
a7029.speech: Said the donation of the machine was a development which marked a significant step forward in the commitment to enhancing healthcare services and bolstering the capacity to combat infectious diseases in the state.

a7029.speaker: Suzanne Theroux, Acting Country Director, US CDC-Nigeria
a7029.name: Suzanne Theroux
a7029.title: Acting Country Director, US CDC-Nigeria
a7029.speech: At the commissioning of the project, presented a laboratory accreditation certificate number ISO15189:2012 to the medical director of FMC, Professor Joseph Kortor; expressed confidence that the donation would improve healthcare for HIV patients and others suffering from chronic diseases.

a7367.speaker: Cicero
a7367.name: Cicero
a7367.speech: "Pecunia nervus belli (money is the sinew of war)."

a7445.speaker: Befia Jalison, 45-year-old resident of Nankhumwa Village
a7445.name: Befia Jalison
a7445.title: 45-year-old resident of Nankhumwa Village
a7445.speech: Explains how difficult it once was to put food on the table. "For the first time, three-quarters of the people here can afford to eat three meals a day," ; "Crime has gone down. Even our houses look different. You see iron sheets everywhere now. Things are good now. Really good," she adds.

a7445.speaker: Bertha Billiat, 60-year-old tomato and maize farmer
a7445.name: Bertha Billiat
a7445.title: 60-year-old tomato and maize farmer
a7445.speech: "Now, I make K80,000. My husband and I decided to buy fertiliser and start keeping livestock. In two years, we will have five cattle and some pigs," Billiat says. She has also introduced crop rotation to her fields and has harvested five bags from winter cropping for the first time; she no longer worries about thieves stealing her harvest and she feels empowered by receiving money directly into her account.

a7445.speaker: Lucy Joseph, housemaid in Manja, Blantyre
a7445.name: Lucy Joseph
a7445.title: housemaid in Manja, Blantyre
a7445.speech: "Before, life was so difficult. Now my mother can buy food and she has started a small business," she says.

a7445.speaker: Village Head Mwamadi, local leader
a7445.name: Village Head Mwamadi
a7445.title: local leader
a7445.speech: Says the entire community has been transformed. "I reroofed my house, which was leaking during the rainy season. I managed to buy a motorbike and I even managed to buy land," he says; adds that it is now easy to tell parents to send their children to school because they can afford it; states that hunger and crime have both sharply declined and disputes are easier to resolve; notes that domestic violence often occurs when men lack income and expresses hope that new economic opportunities would reduce tension in households.

a7445.speaker: Ketelena Witness, village resident
a7445.name: Ketelena Witness
a7445.title: village resident
a7445.speech: "John Kholowo now has green iron sheets on his roof," she says. "We are helping each other buy roofing sheets."

a7445.speaker: Martin Kalima, External Relations Senior Manager at GiveDirectly
a7445.name: Martin Kalima
a7445.title: External Relations Senior Manager at GiveDirectly
a7445.speech: "Our aim is to lift every person in Malawi above the extreme poverty line. We believe people know best what they need. We simply give them the resources and the dignity to decide for themselves."
